We’re currently seeking for an internship position in the Data Processing Developer Technology team. Would you enjoy researching parallel algorithms to accelerate AI and Data Processing workloads on advanced computer architectures? Do you find it rewarding to identify and eliminate system bottlenecks to achieve the best possible performance on pioneering computer hardware? Could you be thrilled about an opportunity to partner with the developer community, working at the forefront of technology breakthroughs that contribute to the success of an industry leader like NVIDIA? If so, we invite you to consider an internship with the Developer Technology Team.
 
 What you will be doing: 
 In this position, you will research and develop techniques to GPU accelerate workloads in deep learning, machine learning or other AI domains.

 Work directly with other technical experts in their fields (industry and academia) to perform in-depth analysis and optimization of complex AI and HPC algorithms to ensure optimal AI solutions on modern CPU and GPU architectures.

 Publish and/or present discovered optimization techniques in developer blogs or relevant conferences to engage and educate the developer community.

 Influence the design of next-generation hardware architectures, software, and programming models in collaboration with research, hardware, system software, libraries, and tools teams at NVIDIA.

 
 What we need to see: 
 Currently pursuing a PhD or Master degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related computationally focused science degree.

 Programming fluency in C/C++ with a deep understanding of algorithms and software development.

 A background that includes parallel programming, e.g., CUDA, OpenACC, OpenMP, MPI, pthreads, etc.

 Effective communication and organization skills, with a logical approach to problem solving, good time management, and prioritization skills.

 
 Ways to stand out from the crowd: 
 Expertise in parallelization and performance optimization of Deep Learning models arising from Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, Recommender Systems, etc.

 Excellent understanding of linear algebra.

 
NVIDIA is committed to fostering a diverse work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.
 
 Applications will be accepted until November 8, 2026 . 
 
 Please note: We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis as they are submitted. Strong candidates may be contacted for next steps before the application deadline. We encourage you to apply early.

Job Description Summary 
In the 12-month Manufacturing Engineering Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience covering all aspects of manufacturing engineering from production to Lean Six Sigma through research and development. 
 
 Job Description 
 About GE Aerospace 
 
 Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world! 
 
 Manufacturing is key to our work at GE Aerospace. Consistently going above and beyond, our Manufacturing teams organize and direct the production of components and assemblies to the highest standards. If you want a hands-on opportunity to advance flight for future generations, this is the team for you. 
 
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 
 We have several placement roles within Manufacturing Engineering: 
 
 Manufacturing Engineering – Power (Cheltenham ) - you’ll be defining and controlling production processes, including the required tooling and equipment; validating design specifications and the implementation of new products, tools, and equipment on the shop floor; and driving accountability through regular operating rhythms to ensure manufacturing engineering activities support production needs. The role evaluates and enhances quality control processes, analyses and reports on production performance (including methods, schedules, downtime, cycle times, machine availability, and waste), and acts as a key stakeholder in the selection and approval of new equipment in line with best practices. It also ensures compliance with relevant policies and regulations, coordinates maintenance and repair activities to keep equipment operational, and identifies and leads improvement projects that deliver cost savings and reductions in direct labour time. 

 Project Manufacturing Engineering (Cheltenham) - contribute to Manufacturing Engineering activities and projects, supported by structured technical training in areas such as Lean, Six Sigma, Statistical Process Control, problem solving, PFMEA, value stream mapping, process flow diagramming, root cause analysis, mechanical concepts, and materials behaviour. In line with our 2027 roadmap, they will participate in projects. You will also help develop Standard Operating Procedures and support local process improvement (Kaizen) initiatives. Throughout the placement, their learning and project involvement. 

 NPI Manufacturing Engineering (Dowty) - y ou will gain hands ‑ on experience across the full spectrum of manufacturing engineering, from production and Lean Six Sigma to research and development. You will support activities such as engineering design, production planning, materials management, cost ‑ reduction projects, problem solving, and the introduction of new products and technologies, including 3D printing and advanced manufacturing methods. Typical responsibilities can include helping to introduce and prototype new technologies, tracking New Product Introduction projects and their impact on business growth, working closely with shop floor teams and other departments to coordinate production and logistics, collecting and analysing data on labour, process stability, and performance metrics, supporting yield improvement initiatives with metallic and composite manufacturing teams, designing tooling and prototypes using CAD/3D modelling software, standardising documentation to improve efficiency and sharing of best practices, and building a strong understanding of shop floor processes and how they interconnect. 

 
 You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK. 
 
 This Manufacturing Engineering team opportunity is offered in our Cheltenham and Gloucester (Dowty, a GE Aerospace company) sites , during the process we will ask you to share your location and team preferences. 
 
 Please identify the location that suits you best based on geography but also based on what the site does. 
 
 With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy . 
 
 Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge. Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come. 
 
 At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential.   
 Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight.   
 
 Dowty, a GE Aerospace company , is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for A wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft. 
 
 Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De-Haviland, Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J. 
 
 Operated by a highly skilled workforce, Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976; and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers 
 
 If you are passionate about Manufacturing Engineering, we would like to hear from you. 
 
 This placement role is an intended pipeline for our Operations Management Leadership Programme (OMLP) which is based across many of our UK sites or our Manufacturing Engineering Leadership Programme (MEDP ). Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to secure a role prior to the end of their placement year. 
 
 Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above! 
 
 Qualifications/Requirements 
 
 Currently studying an E ngineering related bachelor’s or an integrated master’s degree including Manufacturing, Aerospace/Aeronautical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Mechanical Design (Engineering), Materials Science & Engineering, Robotics and Mechatronics or General Engineering 

 On course t to achieve a 2:1 degree or above 

 3 D printing and CAD design is a plus 

 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement 

 
 Desired Characteristics 
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects 

 Organised & able to work towards deadlines 

 Inspired and curious to learn 

 Strong verbal and written communication skills 

 Able to take ownership for projects 

 Analytical and problem-solving skills 

 Proficient in Microsoft Office 

 Able to work as part of a team 

 
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact. 
 
 Total Reward  
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.    
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs.   
    
 Non-contributory Pension              

 Life Assurance   

 Group income protection                

 Private medical cover        

 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell   

 
 Recruitment Process   
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com .  
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31 st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.  
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too. 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS . 
 
 Right to Work   
 
 Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. 
 
 Further, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website .   
 
 Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward.

Software Engineering Internship (Placement Year) 
 
 
This role has been designed as 'Hybrid' with a requirement that you will work on average 2 days per week from an HPE office. 
 
 Who We Are: 
 Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.
 
 
 Job Description: 
 
 Join HPE for a 13-month placement beginning in July 2027. 

 As a Software Engineering Intern at HPE, you’ll gain real-world experience by contributing to business-critical projects and working with cutting-edge technologies. You’ll take ownership of meaningful work, learn from experienced leaders, and connect with other interns. The programme also offers professional development, networking opportunities, volunteering, and event planning. 

 Start date: July 2027 

 Location: Bristol, UK 

 What you’ll do 

 You will build practical experience across the software development lifecycle by contributing to the team’s day-to-day engineering work. Your responsibilities will include: 
 Developing new features 
 Identifying, fixing and documenting bugs 
 Participating in peer code reviews 
 Contributing to the team’s knowledge base 
 Analyzing and designing software and configuration changes 
 You will work closely with QA engineers, DevOps engineers, software developers and architects, gaining insight into how different disciplines collaborate to deliver business-critical software. 
 You will be joining a cohort of interns. Alongside your technical work you will have the opportunity to: 
 Get involved with site charity and social events 
 Develop organizational and leadership skills 
 Support employee resource groups and site-wide initiatives 
 Help shape a strong, inclusive culture across the Bristol site 

 What you’ll need 

 You should currently be pursuing a bachelor’s or integrated master’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, software development or another IT-related field, with your course including a placement year. 
 An interest in one or more of the following areas is desirable: computer architecture; concurrent or multithreaded programming; embedded systems; Linux; networks and communications; cloud microservice development; or operating systems. 
 You must be eligible to work in the UK and available to begin the 13-month placement in early July 2027. 
 Technologies and experience 
 Experience with any of the following programming languages is desirable: assembly or another language used for embedded-system development; C, C# or C++; Java; Python; or Go. 

 What we’d like you to bring 

 On track to receive a 2:1 or higher 
 A proactive approach to learning, problem-solving and delivering high-quality results 
 A collaborative, solution-focused approach to working with others and solving problems 
 Experience taking initiative and contributing positively at university, in the workplace or within your community 
 Comfort with working in a hybrid (virtual and face-to-face) environment 
 Clear communication and presentation skills, with the confidence to ask thoughtful questions 
 
 
 Accessibility 

 HPE is committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace and encourages applications from all qualified individuals, including those with disabilities. If you believe you require accommodation during any stage of the application or interview process, please submit your request by completing our secure form linked here .

 Note: This option is reserved for applicants needing assistance/reasonable accommodation related to a disability. 
 
 
 What We Can Offer You: 
 Health & Wellbeing 
 We strive to provide our team members and their loved ones with a comprehensive suite of benefits that supports their physical, financial and emotional wellbeing.
 
 Personal & Professional Development 
 We also invest in your career because the better you are, the better we all are. We have specific programs catered to helping you reach any career goals you have — whether you want to become a knowledge expert in your field or apply your skills to another division.
 
 Unconditional Inclusion 
 We are unconditionally inclusive in the way we work and celebrate individual uniqueness. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good.
 
 
 Let's Stay Connected: 
 Follow @HPECareers on Instagram to see the latest on people, culture and tech at HPE.

Location: Bristol, UK
 Salary: £2500 per month
 Start date: June 2027
 Application deadline : Midnight, 29th November 2026 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 

 The Internship Programme at Graphcore

 Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.

 What you’ll work on

 Use your programming skills and curiosity to help AI models run efficiently on next-generation Graphcore hardware. 

 In AI Compute Libraries & Performance, you’ll contribute to C++ libraries and compute kernels for machine learning workloads. Your work will include: 

 
 Developing compute kernels: Implement and improve operations such as matrix multiplication (GEMM), convolutions, reductions, elementwise operations and fused kernels that combine multiple operations. 

 Understanding and improving performance: Use profiling and microbenchmarks to measure execution speed and investigate how threading, cache locality, memory layout and kernel launch efficiency affect performance. 

 Checking correctness and reliability: Build regression tests and numerical checks, investigate issues and improve the quality of the libraries our customers use. 

 
 Through these projects, you’ll develop practical experience connecting numerical computing with how code runs on hardware, helping deliver software that is fast, accurate and reliable. 

 Your team and support

 You’ll join a team building high-performance compute libraries that help customers get more from Graphcore hardware. Our work brings together machine learning, numerical computing and accelerator performance, with colleagues sharing their expertise to solve engineering problems.

 You’ll contribute to clearly scoped projects and build your skills with guidance from engineers working in performance and low-level software. Together, we use profiling, experiments and technical reviews to compare approaches, understand trade-offs and improve our solutions. 

 Your buddy will help you settle in, get familiar with our tools and ways of working, and find the right people to ask. Your manager will meet with you regularly to agree goals, offer feedback and discuss your development, including time for learning. 

 We welcome different perspectives and make space for everyone to contribute. Questions, alternative approaches and requests for help are part of how we work. As you take on more responsibility, your colleagues will help you work through challenges, and your ideas will be listened to and discussed respectfully. 

 How you’ll learn and grow

 Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build performance engineering skills through hands-on work on compute kernels, benchmarks and tests. 

 Profiling and experiments will help you understand where time is spent and how changes to code and data layout affect performance. Numerical validation and regression testing will show you how to check that an optimisation preserves correct results and continues to work as software changes. 

 Working with specialists and discussing technical trade-offs will help you develop your engineering judgement, explain your findings and connect mathematical operations to efficient implementations on hardware. 

 What we're looking for

 
 Currently studying towards a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Maths, Machine Learning, Data Science or a related field

 Experience with C or C++11, plus familiarity with Python or scripting tools for automation and testing

 An understanding of linear algebra, numerical methods or scientific computing

 Problem-solving skills and collaborative approach to unfamiliar technical challenges

 
 Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned.

 Coursework or experience with machine learning frameworks, parallel programming, code optimisation, maths libraries or performance analysis would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements.

 Benefits

 
 Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work

 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship

 Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista

 Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform

 
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

 We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.

 Sponsorship

 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.

 Introduction to Graphcore

 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.
Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.

 How to apply and what to expect 

 To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.

 Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.

 The Internship Programme at Graphcore

 Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.

 What you’ll be doing

 Put your engineering foundations to work exploring the electronic hardware behind Graphcore’s AI compute platforms.

 Your internship could focus on Hardware Design, Signal Integrity or elements of both, depending on your interests, the available projects and how your strengths develop. You’ll contribute to a clearly scoped design, analysis, validation or debugging task, with guidance as you work towards a conclusion supported by evidence.

 In Hardware Design, your tasks could include schematic and circuit design, component evaluation, PCB development, board bring-up or laboratory testing. You could help check power rails and clocks, exercise interfaces, investigate faults or develop test and debug access.

 In Signal Integrity, you could explore high-speed links such as PCIe and Ethernet, DDR and other memory interfaces, or clocks and timing-critical signals. Tasks could include reviewing PCB layouts and routing, simulating interconnect behaviour or comparing laboratory measurements with analysis to understand design trade-offs.

 Your team and support

 Hardware Design and Signal Integrity engineers work closely with PCB layout, silicon, validation, firmware, mechanical and thermal engineering, manufacturing and system teams. You’ll see how different engineering perspectives come together to make complex boards work.

 Staff Hardware Engineers and Team Leads will support you with clearly scoped work and regular technical guidance. You can ask for help as you explore unfamiliar concepts, discuss your findings and use feedback to improve your approach.

 Decisions are shaped by simulation, measurement and engineering judgement. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions, speak up and try out ideas early, with support from experienced engineers as you learn.

 How you’ll learn and grow

 Over the 12 weeks, you’ll connect your studies with how boards are designed, analysed, brought up and validated. Your project will help you develop a methodical approach to defining a problem, testing your thinking and explaining what the evidence shows.

 You’ll gain exposure to professional tools such as Mentor Expedition, Ansys HFSS and Keysight ADS, as relevant to your work. Comparing simulations, design choices and laboratory results will help you understand how real hardware behaves and which areas of hardware engineering you’d like to explore further.

 Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated.

 Currently studying towards a degree in Electronic Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics or a closely related technical discipline

 A logical, first-principles approach to unfamiliar problems, with practical engineering experience from university projects, laboratory work, personal projects or activities such as Formula Student, robotics or engineering societies

 Your interests might include schematic design, PCBs, component selection, bring-up, validation, test or fault finding; or transmission lines, impedance, reflections, crosstalk, simulation and electronic measurement.

 Previous industry experience and professional experience with the tools listed above are not required. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned.

 Sponsorship

 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.

 We encourage you to concentrate your efforts on the roles that best align with your skills, interests and university experience, as this will strengthen your application and give you the best chance of success.

 Roles Available in Location : Montrose, Worthing, Stevenage, Ware

 Education required : See individual roles for degree requirements

 This activity is designed to encourage considered applications. Once completed, you'll receive your unique application code required to proceed with your application

 If you have already graduated with a bachelor’s degree and are currently studying a postgraduate Masters, you are not eligible for this programme.

Would you like the opportunity to work in a global energy company? 
 
 Do you enjoy taking on challenging projects? 
 
 Join our innovating Internship Program 
 The Baker Hughes Internship is designed to enable students either pursuing a Bachelors’ or Masters’ degree or recently graduated to gain hands-on work experience as the foundation of their professional lives. Our internships will give you first-hand insights into the processes, systems, and practices that are aligned to ensure customer needs are met through flawless execution and the application of leading-edge technology.
 
 Partner with the best 
 You’ll participate in focused training, and team meetings, work on projects, and present your results. During your internship, you will be supported by a buddy and your manager who will ensure you have a valuable learning experience. You can expect to receive coaching and mentoring to enable you to complete assignments and projects to develop your learning and skillset.
 You will also have the opportunity to become familiar with the Health, Safety, and Environment (HS&E) and culture of Baker Hughes. as well as our strong commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.
 
 As an Intern, you will be responsible for: 
 Completing internal projects to deliver business outcomes and identify process improvement opportunities.
 Learning internal software and tools to support analysis, reporting, and project delivery.
 Collaborating with cross-functional teams and interns to interact and network with global business leaders.
 Applying Health, Safety, and Environment (HS&E) standards and procedures in all situations to ensure compliance is maintained.
 Developing exceptional applications for our business
 Writing clean, scalable code using C#/Type Script programming languages
 Developing end-to-end applications using Angular/.net
 Developing technical interfaces, specifications, and architecture with strong attention to detail
 Applying software development life-cycle principles and methodologies such as Agile and Kanban, to continuously improve our code and processes
 Improving code quality and deployment processes, enhancing CI/CD pipelines undefined
 Working on all aspects of the software engineering discipline
 
 Fuel your passion 
 To be successful in this role you will:
 Be currently enrolled or recently graduated in a Bachelors’ or Masters’ level degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or related programme.
 Have maintained a GPA grade greater than or equal to 3.0 out of 4.0 or the equivalent in your country.
 Demonstrate understanding of working with Back-End development frameworks such as C# / .net
 Demonstrate understanding of Front-End development frameworks such as Angular, React, Vue
 Display knowledge of Relational/NoSQL databases such as SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB
 Be fluent in oral and written English and have effective communication skills.
 Have good interpersonal and leadership skills.
 Be able to legally work in the country that you are applying in, without company sponsorship or time restriction.
 
 Work in a way that works for you 
 We recognize that everyone is different and that the way in which people want to work and deliver at their best is different for everyone. In this role, we may be able to offer flexible working patterns. Talk to us about your desired working options when you apply.
 
 Working with us 
 Working at Baker Hughes means being at the forefront of the energy transition. Our people are diverse, ambitious, and collaborative. We're on a mission to redefine the energy sector by unlocking the power of engineering, data, and science.

Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?

 About Analog Devices 
 Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X .

 At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network.

 ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees.

 At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles.

 Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.

 
 The High-Speed SAR ADC Group in Newbury, UK, has an established reputation for developing industry-leading high-speed, precision analog-to-digital (A/D) converters. The group has been responsible for the development of several flagship SAR ADCs, including the AD7626, AD7960, AD4020, AD4696, AD4080, and AD4880. Its engineers have also published extensively in leading journals and conferences, including IEEE JSSC, ISSCC, ESSERC, the VLSI Symposium, and IEEE TCAS.

 As an intern, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the design, verification, layout, and evaluation of analog and mixed-signal circuits used in precision A/D converters. You will work alongside a highly skilled team of engineers, gaining hands-on experience with real-world IC design challenges and contributing to the development of our next generation of products.
 This role offers an excellent opportunity to develop practical experience in analog and mixed-signal IC design, while learning from experienced engineers in a collaborative development environment. The position is available for internship durations ranging from 3 to 12 months.
 
 Core Responsibilities 
 
 Design of circuits to be used in high precision (16-20bit resolution, >10MSps) analog to digital (A/D) converters
 Verification of the designed circuits with A/D converter

Cambridge, UK | Full-time | Fixed-term, 10–12 weeks | Hybrid

 Salary: £30,000–£35,000 per annum, depending on experience, paid pro rata for the internship duration.

 About us 

 Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion. 

 Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.  

 About the role 

 Our full-time summer internships give current students in technical fields the opportunity to apply their skills and expertise in an industrial setting. 

 You will join us at our head office in Cambridge, UK, for 10 to 12 weeks, working alongside talented software and hardware engineers, mathematicians, quantum information theorists and physicists who are experts in their fields. 

 You will have a dedicated supervisor and work on a project designed to make the best use of your existing skills while developing your knowledge of quantum computing and quantum error correction. We will support you in producing a meaningful piece of work that you can be proud of by the end of your internship. 

 Previous interns have committed code to industry-standard open-source compilers, co-authored research papers and led the design of new software tools. 

 What you will do 

 
 
 Design, develop and test software that contributes to Riverlane’s quantum error correction technology.



 
 
 Work closely with colleagues across software engineering, research and other technical disciplines 

 
 
 Explore ideas, evaluate different approaches and contribute to technical problem-solving 

 Communicate your work clearly through discussions, presentations and written reports 

 Develop your understanding of quantum computers, quantum error correction and their potential applications 

 
 What we need 

 
 
 You must be a current student at the time of application, studying towards a Bachelor’s degree (second year or later), Master’s degree or PhD.



 
 You must be studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Electronic Engineering or another related technical subject.



 
 Experience using at least one general-purpose programming language, demonstrated through coursework, personal projects or research.



 
 An understanding of core programming concepts, including data structures and algorithms.



 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.



 
 Clear written and verbal communication skills.



 
 The ability to take initiative and work effectively as part of a team.



 
 An interest in applying your software skills to quantum computing; prior quantum computing knowledge or experience is not required.



 
 Availability to work full-time for 10–12 weeks.



 
 Even better if… 

 
 
 You have experience with C++ or Python, the main languages you will use during the internship.



 
 You have experience writing tests, debugging code or using version control tools such as Git.



 
 You have developed software as part of a collaborative project.



 
 Important notes 

 
 
 You must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the internship. If you hold a UK student visa, please check that its conditions allow you to undertake this full-time internship.



 
 
 PhD students may need to temporarily step away from their PhD to complete the internship. This may affect their right-to-work status, and applicants should check their individual circumstances 

 
 
 You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks during the summer vacation period 

 
 
 You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of any intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane 

 Internships are based at our head office in Cambridge, UK 

 
 How to apply 

 Please upload a CV and covering letter through our careers page. Your CV should include the grades you have received so far in your degree(s). Your covering letter should explain why you are applying for the software engineering internship and what skills and experience you would bring.

 Deadline 

 Please submit your application by Friday 6 November 2026 . Interviews will be held in Cambridge, or virtually if required.

 What can you expect from us 

 Alongside a competitive salary, we offer private medical insurance, a health cash plan and life assurance, as well many other benefits. 

 You can also expect a diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 25 different nationalities. 

 If you have any queries, please contact jobs@riverlane. com . Please do not send your applications to this email address, all applications should be submitted via our careers page. 

 Everyone is welcome at Riverlane. We are an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from eligible and suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender reassignment, religion or belief, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, or pregnancy and maternity/paternity. 

 Women and other underrepresented groups may be less likely to apply for a role unless they meet all or nearly all of the requirements. If this applies to you, we still encourage you to apply - you may be a great fit, even if you don’t meet every single qualification. We’d love to hear from you. 

 If you need any adjustments made to the application or selection process so you can do your best, please let us know. We will be happy to help. 

 GDPR notice: Riverlane collects and processes personal data in accordance with applicable data protection laws. If you are a European Job Applicant see the privacy notice for further details.

Location: Bristol, UK 
 Duration: 12 weeks 
 Salary: £2500 per month 
 Start date: June 2027 
 Application deadline: Midnight 29 th November 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 

 The Internship Programme at Graphcore 

 Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence. 

 What you’ll be doing 

 Put your Linux and scripting foundations to work exploring the cloud platforms that support Graphcore’s AI systems. 

 As a Cloud Platform Engineering Intern, you’ll help deploy, test and monitor services across private and public cloud environments. You’ll contribute through clearly scoped tasks, with guidance from experienced engineers as you build confidence. 

 Your tasks could include writing or improving scripts, reviewing metrics and logs, investigating issues and documenting what you learn. You’ll see how automation and monitoring help the team manage high-performance AI infrastructure and how continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) and Infrastructure-as-Code are used in real systems. 

 Your team and support 

 The Cloud Platform team provides large-scale AI systems through private and public cloud services. Its work brings together Graphcore AI systems, industry-standard servers, switches and storage. Some environments use pre-release hardware and software, giving you a view of how new technology becomes usable. 

 You’ll work alongside experienced engineers through sprint activities, technical reviews, project demonstrations and practical investigations. You can ask for help as you learn, share your progress and use feedback to improve your work on defined tasks. 

 Decisions are shaped by evidence, engineering judgement and open discussion. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions early, share what you find and try out ideas, with support from experienced engineers as you learn. 

 How you’ll learn and grow 

 Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build practical experience with Linux systems, scripting, automation and monitoring through the work your tasks focus on. 

 Investigating issues with logs and metrics will help you develop a methodical approach to problem solving and understand how cloud services fit together. Technical reviews and project demonstrations will help you explain your findings, learn from feedback and explore whether platform engineering is a direction you’d like to pursue. 

 Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated. 

 What we’re looking for 

 
 Currently studying towards a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT, Electronic Engineering or a related subject 

 Basic Linux and command-line experience, gained through study, projects or independent learning 

 Some scripting or programming experience, such as Python, Bash or a similar language 

 A methodical approach to investigating technical issues, with clear communication, curiosity and willingness to learn from feedback and take responsibility for defined tasks 

 
 Bring an interest in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, networking, CI/CD, monitoring or computer systems. 

 Previous industry experience is not required . Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects, independent learning or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned. 

 Benefits 

 
 Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work 

 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship 

 Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista 

 Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform 

 
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. 

 We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you. 

 Sponsorship 

 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities. . 

 Introduction to Graphcore 

 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. 

 An internship at Graphcore gives you the chance to explore where your interests and skills could take you. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. Together, you’ll share ideas and solve challenging problems, building experience and confidence to help you decide what comes next. 

 How to apply and what to expect 

 To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring. 

 Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.

 Understanding of ADCs, DACs or delta-sigma conversion.
 Understanding of Class-D amplifiers or other audio signal-chain circuits.
 Familiarity with switched-mode power supplies such as buck, boost or charge-pump converters.

Duration: 12 weeks 
 Salary: £2500 per month 
 Start date: June 2027 
 Applications deadline: Midnight 29 th November 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 

 The Internship Programme at Graphcore 

 Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence. 

 What you’ll work on 

 Put your engineering foundations to work exploring how advanced AI hardware is tested, diagnosed and improved. 

 As a Test Engineering Intern in our Product Test and Diagnosis team, you’ll contribute to practical work across silicon, boards, server blades or rack-scale systems. Depending on your project, you may develop automated test solutions, run system-level tests and analyse the results. 

 Your work will help the team improve how Graphcore tests and understands its products. It’s a chance to see how manufacturing test connects design, validation and performance in use, while contributing to a defined project or set of activities. 

 Your team and support 

 You’ll join the Product Test and Diagnosis team in Bristol, within Manufacturing Operations. The wider team spans Bristol, Cambridge, India, the US and Taiwan, developing test strategies across the full product lifecycle. 

 You’ll work alongside experienced engineers on practical tasks close to the hardware. You can ask for help as you investigate results and develop tools, with support as you take ownership of your project or activities. 

 Decisions are shaped by test results, clear data and thoughtful problem solving. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions, share your findings and try out ideas, with support from experienced engineers as you learn. 

 How you’ll learn and grow 

 Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build practical experience in semiconductor test and diagnosis through the work your project focuses on. 

 Running tests, analysing data and investigating issues will help you connect your studies with real hardware, develop your technical judgement and explain your findings. Working with engineers who improve test tools and processes will give you a clearer view of the areas you enjoy and might want to explore further. 

 Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated. 

 What we’re looking for 

 
 Currently studying for a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Physics, Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience 

 An understanding of electronics or printed circuit board (PCB) fundamentals, with an interest in semiconductor technology, manufacturing, test or validation 

 Programming or scripting experience, ideally with Python 

 The ability to use data to investigate problems and communicate your findings, demonstrated through practical work involving electronics, embedded systems, validation, or automation 

 
 Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through university projects, laboratory work, research, personal projects or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned. 

 Familiarity with Linux, Bash or Git would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements. 

 Benefits 

 
 Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work 

 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship 

 Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista 

 Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform 

 
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. 

 We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you. 

 Sponsorship

 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.

 Introduction to Graphcore

 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.
Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.

 How to apply and what to expect 

 To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.

 Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.

5feebaf35ac8.description:
PsiQuantum’s mission is to build the first useful quantum computers—machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems. 

 Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries. 

 Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry—including partners like GlobalFoundries—we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don’t feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure. 

 In 2024, PsiQuantum announced government-funded projects to support the build-out of our first utility-scale quantum computers in Brisbane, Australia, and Chicago, Illinois. These initiatives reflect a growing recognition that quantum computing will be strategically and economically defining—and that now is the time to scale. 

 PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies—including Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical—to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact. 

 Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift—and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we have a clear path to make it real. 

 Come join us. 

 Job Summary: 

 Our system architecture department sits at the interface of hardware development, manufacturing, and the quantum architecture to design the first fault-tolerant quantum computer. The optical architecture group are specifically responsible for:

 
 discovering and developing new schemes for photonic quantum computation

 translating abstract quantum information protocols into the designs of physical systems

 About the Role 
 As an Analog Design Engineer Intern at Analog Devices (ADI), you will work alongside experienced engineers on the design, simulation, and characterization of high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits (ICs). You will contribute to the development of circuits such as amplifiers, filters, data converters, and clocking solutions, while gaining hands-on experience with industry-standard design and simulation tools including Cadence and SPICE.
 In this role, you will support circuit design, simulation, layout, silicon validation, and laboratory testing activities, developing practical skills across the full IC development lifecycle. This internship offers an excellent opportunity to learn from industry experts and contribute to cutting-edge semiconductor products used in a wide range of applications.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Assist in the design, simulation, and verification of analog and mixed-signal circuits, including amplifiers, filters, and data converters.
 Use industry-standard simulation tools such as SPICE and Cadence to analyse circuit performance and validate design concepts.
 Support IC layout activities with a focus on performance, matching, reliability, and manufacturability.
 Perform laboratory measurements and characterization using equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and power supplies.
 Collaborate with senior engineers to debug design issues, optimize circuit performance, and support silicon bring-up activities.
 Document design results, test findings, and technical analyses in a clear and structured manner.
 Required Skills and Qualifications 
 Fundamental understanding of analog circuit design, including amplifiers, filters, biasing circuits, and feedback systems.
 Basic knowledge of mixed-signal IC design principles and the interaction between analog and digital circuitry.
 Familiarity with circuit simulation and modelling using tools such as SPICE or equivalent EDA tools.
 Understanding of CMOS technologies and semiconductor device fundamentals.
 Exposure to integrated circuit layout concepts, including matching, parasitic effects, and layout best practices.
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
 Effective communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

Job Description Summary 
In the 12-month Systems Engineering Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience in covering all aspects of systems engineering from requirements capturing, system design and verification. 
 
 Job Description 
 About GE Aerospace 
 
 Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft . You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives . Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world! 
 
 Engineering 
 
 Engineering is at the centre of what we do, and we are looking for talented, innovative engineers who can help us design and develop products for today, tomorrow, and in the future. If you are a dreamer, doer, and inventor who wants your voice to be heard and see your ideas take flight, this is the opportunity for you. 
 
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 
 In the 12-month Systems Engineering Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience in covering all aspects of systems engineering from requirements capturing, system design and verification . You could be helping with gaining and maintaining network connectivity and providing support services to customers or process improvement using IT systems internally. 
 
 We have several types or roles in this area: 
 
 Control Systems ( Dowty) - within a multi-disciplinary engineering team at Dowty Propellers, supporting the business in meeting customer requirements, quality, schedule, and cost across new applications, R&D, and in-service product support. Key responsibilities include defining requirements for propeller control systems within industry-standard systems and safety engineering frameworks proposing cost-effective control system solutions and analysing system performance using simulation environments that integrate propeller, engine, and airframe elements. You create requirements for control units for subcontract design and manufacture, define and support verification testing of propeller control systems, contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, and ensure implementation and maintenance of GE Aerospace compliance standards and policies. 

 
 Systems Engineering (Cheltenham) - end-to-end experience of the systems engineering lifecycle for safety-critical aerospace products such as controllers, displays, and aircraft power distribution systems. You will work with customers to capture, write, and manage requirements, ensuring full traceability, and then define and execute verification and validation activities through hands-on lab testing, integration tests, and analysis of results. The role supports certification and safety by contributing to evidence for aviation authorities and working to industry standards. You will collaborate across hardware, software, safety, and certification teams, participate in technical reviews with internal and external stakeholders, and apply lean engineering principles to drive continuous improvement, efficiency, and quality. 

 
 You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK. 
 
 This opportunity is offered in our Cheltenham and Gloucester (Dowty, a GE Aerospace company) sites , during the process we will ask you to share your location and role preferences. 
 
 With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy. 
 
 Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge . Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come. 
 
 At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential. 
 
 Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight.   
 
 Dowty, a GE Aerospace company , is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for A wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft. 
 
 Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De-Haviland, Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J. 
 
 Operated by a highly skilled workforce, Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976; and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers. 
 
 This placement role is an intended pipeline to our Edison Engineering Development Programme (EEDP) based in Cheltenham. Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to secure a role prior to the end of their placement year. 
 
 Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above! 
 
 If you love technology and desire a career in Engineering, EEDP is for you. 
 
 Edison Engineers understand and apply engineering fundamentals in the business environment and design, analyse, and test the technology that continues to innovate how the world flies sustainably. Find out more here https://invent.ge/eedp 
 
 If you are passionate about Systems Engineering, we would love to hear from you. 
 
 Qualifications / Requirements 
 
 Currently pursuing a B achelor’s or integrated M aster’s degree in S ystems E ngineering , Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering , Systems, or Control Systems or a related field 

 Keen interest in Systems Engineering 

 Literate with Microsoft Office tools 

 On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above 

 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement 

 
 Desired Characteristics 
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects 

 Organised & able to work towards deadlines 

 Inspired and curious to learn 

 Strong verbal and written communication skills 

 Able to take ownership for projects 

 Analytical and problem-solving skills 

 Proficient in Microsoft Office 

 Able to work as part of a team 

 
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact. 
 
 Total Reward 
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice , gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible. 
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs. 
   
 Non-contributory Pension 

 Life Assurance 

 Group income protection      

 Private medical cover 

 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell 

 
 Recruitment Process 
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com . 
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31 st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. 
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too. 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS . 
 
 Right to Work 
 
 Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. 
 
 Further, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website. 
 
 Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward.

 This role offers hands-on experience with System Verilog based verification, simulation environments, testbench development, and functional coverage Ideal for students or early-career engineers exploring a path into ASIC/SoC development.

 RTL design principles
 Simulation workflows
 
 Familiarity with scripting languages (Python, Perl, Tcl, Bash, etc.).
 Good analytical and debugging skills.
 Strong communication and willingness to learn in a fast-paced engineering environment.
 Nice-to-Have Skills 
 Experience with UVM-based verification.
 Familiarity with EDA tools (Xcelium, etc.).
 Knowledge of: SoC design concepts
 Bus protocols (AXI, AHB, APB)
 Assertions (SVA)
 Coverage-driven verification
 
 What You Will Learn 
 Industry-standard ASIC/SoC verification methodologies.
 Writing and debugging System Verilog-UVM testbench components.
 Simulation and coverage-driven verification flows.
 Collaboration with digital design, architecture, and modelling teams.
 Why Join Us 
 Gain hands-on verification experience with real silicon IP.
 Work with experienced engineers who provide mentorship and guidance.
 Exposure to modern EDA tools and methodologies.
 Opportunity to convert to full-time/graduate roles.
 Collaborative, learning-driven workplace culture.
