Job Description Summary 
In the 12-month Data Science Placement, you may be combining data and analytics with engineering or applications knowledge. 
 
 Job Description 
 About GE Aerospace 
 
 Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft . You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives . Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world! 
 
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 
 In the 12-month Data Science Placement, you may be combining data and analytics with engineering or applications knowledge. 
 
 GE Aerospace combines unrivalled strength in the Aviation domain with digital capability to provide business changing outcomes. Our Data Science projects include working with GE Commercial Engines to support all aspects of the engines business from in-service deployment, fleet monitoring and management to repairs, supply chain and financial operations. A typical Data Science project starts with a problem statement and dataset, and our job is to work alongside our internal GE customers to develop, test and deploy analytics which solve their problems or provide significant insights to improve to their business impact. We also develop custom in-house analytic tools which help us deliver our projects efficiently and effectively. Every project is different and gives the opportunity to learn something new. The Data Scientist role combines data and analytics with engineering or applications knowledge. We make extensive use of AI, Machine Learning and Advanced Analytics including Computer Vision; Neural Networks; Multivariate Modelling, Anomaly Detection; Segmentation; NLP; Bayesian Reasoning, as well as working with wide-ranging and big data sets. 
 
 Every project is different and gives the opportunity to learn something new. 
 
 Responsibilities Include 
 
 Applying analytical or ML methods to monitor trends and identify issues 

 Assisting in the development, test and deployment of analytics including dashboards/reports and the maintenance of existing capabilities 

 Assisting in the preparation of clear and insightful presentations 

 A structured approach to problem solving 

 Ability to deliver required tasks to timelines 

 Comfortable working within a team or independently 

 Communicating technical information to a range of stakeholders – e.g., peers, experts and non-experts, customers. 

 Our Data Science projects vary from site to site, specific project details will be provided at the interview stage 

 
 You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK.  
 
 This opportunity is offered in our Eastleigh site . 
 
 GE Aerospace, Eastleigh is a small, friendly office (c 65 employees) located in Chandlers Ford, within easy walking distance of local railway and bus links. With a deep history of developing and supplying condition monitoring technology and products to the aerospace sector, GE Aerospace Eastleigh combines unrivalled strength in the Aviation domain with digital capability to provide business changing outcomes. We are seeking highly motivated individuals to contribute to our digital future and have been successfully running internships since 2018. The site has opportunities in Data Science. Our job is to work alongside Aviation customers to develop, test and deploy analytics or software which solve their problems or provide significant insights and improvements to their business. We also develop custom in-house tools to help us deliver our projects efficiently and effectively. We support a wide range of customers both internal and external to GE. Every project is different and gives the opportunity to learn something new. 
 
 This placement role is an intended pipeline for our Digital Technology Leadership Programme (DTLP) based in Cheltenham . Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to secure a role prior to the end of their placement year. 
 
 Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above! 
 
 If you are passionate about Data Science, we would like to hear from you. 
 
 Qualifications/Requirements 
 
 Currently studying a Maths, Physics, Physical/Engineering Sciences, Data Science, Computer Science, or Mechanical/ Aeronautical Engineering Bachelor’s or integrated Master’s degree. 

 On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above. 

 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement. 

 Analytical scripting skills – Python preferred. 

 Some knowledge or awareness of AI/ ML/ Advanced statistics methods . 

 SQL and Version Control (e.g., GitHub) experience also useful. 

 A keen interest in Data Science and analytics and working in Aerospace . 

 
 Desired Characteristics 
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects 

 Organised & able to work towards deadlines 

 Inspired and curious to learn 

 Strong verbal and written communication skills 

 Able to take ownership for projects 

 Analytical and problem-solving skills 

 Proficient in Microsoft Office 

 Able to work as part of a team 

 
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact. 
 
 Total Reward 
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice , gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.    
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs. 
   
 Non-contributory Pension 

 Life Assurance 

 Group income protection 

 Private medical cover 

 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell 

 
 Recruitment Process 
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com. 
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31 st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. 
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too. 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS . 
 
 Right to Work 
 
 Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. 
 
 Further, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website. 
 
 Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward.

84b88b8b51d1.description:
Join us, be part of more. 
 
 We’re so much more than an energy company. We’re a family of brands revolutionising how we power the planet. We're energisers. One team of 21,000 colleagues that's energising a greener, fairer future by creating an energy system that doesn’t rely on fossil fuels, whilst living our powerful commitment to igniting positive change in our communities. Here, you can find more purpose, more passion, and more potential. That’s why working here is #MoreThanACareer. We do energy differently - we do it all. We make it, store it, move it, sell it, and mend it. 
 
 At Centrica, we're not just adapting to the future of energy, we're shaping it – and we’re looking for curious minds, fresh perspectives, and ambitious early talent to help us make it happen. As a Technology Intern, you'll spend a year gaining hands-on experience and working on meaningful projects that contribute to real business outcomes. From day one, you'll be part of the team, tackling genuine challenges and building valuable technical and professional skills. It's an opportunity to put your learning into practice, develop future-ready skills and gain insight into where a career in Technology could take you. 
 
 Why Technology? 
 
 From AI and automation to cyber security and cloud engineering, technology is powering the solutions that will help create a more sustainable future. 
 During your Year in Industry, you’ll gain hands-on experience in an area such as AI and Data Science, Cyber Security, Software Development, Cloud Engineering, Digital Products, Platform Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, Innovation, or Integrations. You’ll contribute to real work and projects, learn from experienced colleagues, and develop practical, future-ready skills. It’s an opportunity to apply what you’re learning at university, explore how technology can solve real business challenges and discover where a future career in Tech could take you. 
 
 Support to help you thrive 
 
 We're looking for potential, not perfection. 
 That's why you'll be supported every step of the way through structured development opportunities, experienced mentors and line managers, dedicated graduate learning, buddy support and a network of graduates from across the business. 
 With offices across the UK and a hybrid approach to working, flexibility is an important part of our graduate and intern programmes. You’ll need to be open to travel when required and, for some placements, relocation, giving you the opportunity to experience different teams, locations, and parts of our business. 
 
 What we need from you: 
 Expecting a minimum 2:1 degree (2:2 if combined with a Master's) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Cyber Security, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Mathematics, or a related discipline 
 Right to work in the UK
 Curious, proactive, and keen to learn 
 Willingness to travel and relocate where required 
 Available to start in June 2027  
 
 Here's what's in it for you: 
 Annual salary of £24,539.00
 12-months hands-on experience working in a dedicated area of Tech 
 Structured support and development throughout your placement 
 Opportunities to learn from experienced professionals and build your network 
 The chance to make a meaningful contribution while developing skills that will support your future career 
 
 
 Why should you apply?   
  
We’re not a perfect place – but we’re a people place. Our priority is supporting all of the different realities our people face. Life is about so much more than work. We get it. That’s why we’ve designed our total rewards to give you the flexibility to choose what you need, when you need it, making sure that you and your family are supported not only financially, but physically and emotionally too. Visit the link below to discover why we’re a great place to work and what being part of more means for you.  
  
 https://www.morethanacareer.energy/centrica 
   
 If you're full of energy, fired up about sustainability, and ready to craft not only a better tomorrow, but a better you, then come and find your purpose in a team where your voice matters, your growth is non-negotiable, and your ambitions are our priority.
 
Help us, help you. We would love for you to share any information about yourself throughout our recruitment process so that we can better understand you and help shape your journey.

86851580ccbc.description:
Intern - Student Engineer (Systems Eng) 
 
 Company: 
Boeing Defence United Kingdom Limited 
 
 Overview: 
 This post is for a Systems Engineering Intern to work within the engineering function in Boeing Defence UK (BDUK) ideally based in Bristol but with an option for basing it in Frimley, Yoevil or Gosport for the right candidate. BDUK is a subsidiary of the Boeing Company and currently employs over 2,000 people in the UK. BDUK is responsible for delivering several exciting contracts to our UK defence customers including E-7 AEW&C, P-8A Maritime Patrol Aircraft, C4ISR Services, Through Life Support for the Chinook & Apache Fleets, Logistic Information Services and Training Services.

 The Department that Systems Engineering, Integration and Test (SEIT) falls under comprises a numbers of capabilities providing people, process and tools into programmes across the business. The capabilities are: Requirements; Modelling and Architecture; Verification and Validation; Simulation and Analysis; Product Lifecycle Management and Engineering Business Operations; Strategy and Internal Capability Development projects (e.g. Digital Engineering).

 Position Responsibilities: 
 As a member of the SEIT team, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to work on a one or more programmes and business development opportunities within the Fixed Wing, Vertical Life or Digital and Digital Programmes Business Units and additionally contribute to engineering excellence across the company. They may also have the opportunity to work for other teams within the department depending on business needs.

 The successful candidate for this position will be responsible to a SEIT Technical Lead on the allocated scope of work. They will be involved with technical management and design of systems solutions, system integration and providing support in order to facilitate the delivery of milestones within time and budget, and maintaining customer satisfaction.

 The role is fundamental in translating customer needs/requirements into appropriate solutions. It requires the successful candidate to work in multidisciplinary teams to generate proposals and develop deliverable solutions.

 The role will include working autonomously and as part of various teams and may involve interaction with other parts of Boeing and our suppliers.

 Key Tasks include: 
 Determining, evolving and managing stakeholder requirements
 System Design including aspects of: Concept generation, Functional analysis using techniques such as Model Based Systems Engineering, Interface Management, Maintaining Design Integrity, Modelling and Simulation, Selecting Preferred Solutions, Integration & Verification, Validation and Transition to Operation
 Systems Engineering Management, including: Project Planning, Monitoring and Control, tailoring of generic processes, input to technical risks and opportunities
 The application of the fundamental concepts of systems thinking to systems engineering. These include: understanding what a system is; its context within its environment; its boundaries and interfaces; its lifecycle and an appreciation of the role the system plays in the super system of which it is a part.
 The tailoring and application of engineering initiatives, best practices and processes.
 
 Basic Qualifications: 
 Right to work in UK - We do not sponsor applicants for employment visa status.
 
 Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience): 
 Aiming for MEng/BEng in an engineering related subject
 Candidates should be studying for a degree in Engineering.
 Experience with Software will be an advantage.
 Candidates should also have excellent communication and team working skills and a proactive approach to work.
 Typical Education & Experience: 
 Systems, Computing, Engineering and associated subjects
 
 Relocation: 
 This position does not offer relocation. Candidates must live in the immediate area or relocate at their own expense.
 Work Authorization :
 This requisition is for a locally hired position in the UK. Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work immediately in the United Kingdom. Boeing will not attempt to obtain Immigration and labour sponsorship for any applicants. Benefits and pay are determined at the local level and are not part of Boeing U.S. based payroll.
 PLEASE NOTE: 
 The successful candidate will be expected to undergo an Intrusive Security Clearance Process, which will require 5 years uninterrupted residency in the UK prior to applying.
 We do not sponsor applicants for employment visa status.
 
 
 Language Requirements: 
 
Not Applicable 
 
 Education: 
Not Applicable 
 
 Relocation: 
Relocation assistance is not a negotiable benefit for this position. 
 
 Security Clearance: 
This position requires the ability to acquire a UK Secret security Clearance for which the UK Government requires UK residency. The successful candidate will hold, or have the ability to acquire, Security Clearance (SC). 
 
 Visa Sponsorship: 
Employer will not sponsor applicants for employment visa status. 
 
 Contingent Upon Award Program 
This position is not contingent upon program award 
 
 Shift: 
Not a Shift Worker (United Kingdom)

8691f9e42b9d.description:
Choose Wisely, Apply Confidently 
 
 To maximize your opportunities at securing an Industrial Placement with us this year, we strongly advise that you apply to no more than 3 adverts . (For clarity, multiple roles within a single advert are considered one application.)

 We encourage you to concentrate your efforts on the roles that best align with your skills, interests and university experience, as this will strengthen your application and give you the best chance of success.

 Roles Available in Location : Barnard Castle, Worthing, GSK HQ London, Ware, Montrose

 Education required : See individual roles for degree requirements

 Please read the degree requirements for each role carefully before applying. 

 Other requirements : You will have completed a minimum of 2 years of your undergraduate degree but will not have graduated at the start of your placement. You must be enrolled at a UK (United Kingdom) or ROI (Republic of Ireland) University for the duration of your placement.

 Pre-application activity: Before applying, you'll need to obtain an application code by completing a short activity in Connectr, our candidate engagement platform.

 This activity is designed to encourage considered applications. Once completed, you'll receive your unique application code required to proceed with your application.

 If you have already graduated with a bachelor’s degree and are currently studying a postgraduate Masters, you are not eligible for this programme. 

 Language requirement : Written and spoken fluency in English

 Expected Start date : July 2027

 Duration : 1 year (approximately)

 Salary : £28,900 (London) or £26,400 (all other areas) plus a bonus.

 Workplace Arrangements: Please read the workplace arrangements for each role carefully before applying.

 Application Closing : Roles are expected to close on 22/10/2026 , however, candidates will be reviewed regularly, and the advert may close at any point. Please ensure you review and complete the application stages below. 

 Are you looking to gain valuable real world work experience and help positively impact the lives of others? 

 A GSK internship offers you the opportunity to kickstart your career – to take on a real role with genuine impact. You’ll take on challenging tasks within live projects or assignments. You’ll also get to learn from others in your team and other parts of GSK whilst developing your skills and gaining valuable experience for wherever the future takes you.

 What do we offer you? 
 A competitive salary, with an annual bonus based on company performance.
 Employee recognition programs, which reward exceptional achievements.
 Access to our cutting-edge wellbeing platform: personalize your experience, help reduce stress, increase focus, build connections and resilience. You will also have access to a confidential helpline 24/7, mindfulness, health screenings and financial wellbeing support. 
 Access to Private Healthcare Insurance, including 24-hour access to an online GP.
 Optional Support: Includes identity protection, long-term care insurance, home, auto, and pet insurance
 Opportunities to work with Employee Resource Groups, providing opportunities to network, gain mentorship, and develop personally and professionally.
 Access to IPUnite which is a community of Early Careers programme participants offering development, networking and social connections to help you make the best of your programme. You will also be invited to join LinkedIn groups and pre-joining webinars, to enable you to connect and network with new students.
 2 volunteering days per year
 
 Typical skills you can expect to learn on this placement will include:
 Teamworking through working with multidisciplinary teams
 Communication (written & verbal)
 Time management
 Problem-solving
 Networking
 Data analysis and management
 Technical skills (detailed within each role description)
 
 The Roles (7 available) 

 This advert contains multiple roles. Please read each role carefully before proceeding as you will be asked to provide a preference later in the application process. 

 Role 1 – Logistics Shared Services & Supply Chain – Barnard Castle 
 
 Degree requirements: Biomedical Sciences, Any Engineering or Life-Sciences Supply Chain + Business but open to any degree

 Workplace Arrangements: Full time on site required

 Overview of the Department 
 Barnard Castle is a key secondary manufacturing site for GSK, supporting a diverse portfolio of pharmaceutical products ranging from sterile syringes and vials to liquid inhalations and dermatological products. The site plays an important role in the development and launch of new products, with a strong focus on operational excellence and continuous improvement. Recently, Barnard Castle expanded its capabilities with the opening of a state-of-the-art aseptic digital facility producing biopharmaceuticals. The Logistics Shared Services & Supply Chain team supports the efficient flow of materials across the site and works collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to ensure supply continuity.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 Engage in warehouse inbound and outbound activities
 Provide guidance and support for departments, global suppliers and contractors
 Support new equipment introduction and new process implementation
 Simplification and automation of our material scheduling processes
 Data analysis of warehouse capacity and reporting on budget
 Demand review (including gathering and understanding market intelligence on forecasts and supply chain complexities)
 Assess inventory policy for consumable materials
 Data quality improvements
 
 Role 2 - GSK Production System - Worthing 
 
 Degree requirements: Engineering, Supply chain, Pharmaceuticals Science

 Workplace Arrangements: Full time on site required

 Overview of the Department 
 GPS (GlaxoSmithKline Production System) is GSKs system for deploying Lean Sigma methodologies to drive business performance. Practitioners deploy the OneGPS system effectively through the site based on business needs, collaborating closely with the Site Leadership Teams and aligned Value Stream Directors (VSD). As a GPS Practitioner, you will coach and facilitate the embedding of the GPS standards so that work as a system to improve and support business performance. Key to this is GSK Industrial Placement UK Programme Pharmaceutical Business and Supply Chain (Multiple Roles & Locations) Industrial Placement, UK 2026 supporting the change management for enhancing our problem-solving capabilities and continuous improvement mindset.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 The Site GPS team is accountable for deploying and embedding the GSK Production System to deliver the Business Strategy and improving Business Performance (Quality, Safety, Service, Cost, and Innovation).
 Supports site teams in GPS roll-out; making sure that GPS is being used to develop the capability of all the Site personnel to implement day to day continuous improvement activities.
 Helps to ensure the day-to-day continuous improvement activities result in a continuous improvement in the Site Performance towards the goal of Zero Accidents, Zero Defects and Zero Waste.
 Conducts ‘self-assessment’ of the Site vs. the GPS Maturity matrices and supports the site to close any gaps.
 Coaches and trains Site teams in GPS.
 
 Role 3 - Supply and Logistics - Worthing 
 
 Degree requirements: Engineering (accredited), Business, Maths, Science, Supply Chain based degree, Business or Supply Chain, Engineering, Economics or Data Analytics.

 Workplace Arrangements: Flexible working via performance with choice (office & home working may be available)

 Overview of the Department 
 The scheduling team within the Supply & Logistics department at the Worthing site is integral to the efficient functioning of the site’s supply chain. This team oversees the planning and procurement of incoming materials to support manufacturing schedules and manages production timelines, ensuring that finished goods are prepared for shipment in a timely manner. Their responsibilities include developing plans that meet supply chain demands while operating within established capacities, thereby optimizing workflows, reducing delays, and ensuring a consistent supply of products to patients and customers globally. Placement participants will gain exposure and interaction across all site functions, providing valuable insights into a broad array of operational processes.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 Assist with inventory management and incoming material planning to identify and address at-risk stock (slow-moving and obsolete items) and coordinate with key functions to prevent future issues.
 Support cross-functional engagement to facilitate the batch tracker process, ensuring alignment between Supply & Logistics, Manufacturing, QC Testing (Chemistry and Microbiology), and other site functions.
 Participate in scheduling and cross-functional meetings, providing support with facilitation, issue resolution, and collaborative problem-solving across departments.
 Support and develop material planning standard work, helping to drive consistency, efficiency, and adherence to planning processes.
 Gain exposure to QC Testing operations, including Chemistry, Microbiology, and Incoming Materials testing, understanding how laboratory activities impact production scheduling and product release timelines.
 Develop digital solutions to simplify and automate existing scheduler and supply chain processes, utilizing tools such as AI, Power BI, and Power Apps.
 Work on digital improvement projects and provide troubleshooting support where required, helping to enhance operational performance and data visibility across the department.
 Oversee progress in relation to Supply & Logistics objectives and KPIs and provide support for project execution.
 Participate in and drive continuous improvement initiatives across the department and site to streamline processes and reduce waste.
 Gain an understanding of supply chain principles, quality operations, and the application of analytical thinking to business situations and scenarios.
 This keeps the role focused on Supply & Logistics while clearly integrating the additional QC, material planning, batch tracking, and digital project responsibilities.

 Role 4 - External Manufacturing – GSK HQ 
 
 Degree requirements: Engineering, Business, Science, Economics, Supply Chain, Data Analytics, Digital

 Workplace Arrangements: Flexible working via performance with choice (office & home working may be available)

 Overview of the Department 
 Global Supply Chain management is all about ensuring we can supply our lifesaving and life-enhancing products to people around the globe, but making sure that the right products arrive at the right time in the right place is no easy task. We offer a variety of supply chain placements, from forecasting demand, production planning, raw materials management, and data analytics, to warehousing and supply chain logistics. Whichever role you undertake, you’ll be fully immersed in the day-to-day and future plans of the role and in playing a key part in ensuring our products reach our patients and consumers in an efficient and timely manner.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 Leading and delivering improvement projects
 Working with suppliers, customers and colleagues from around the world
 Distribution chains for complex products that require changing temperature for sensitive goods
 Building strong relationships with key third party suppliers
 Risk Management, Data analysis, intelligence & reporting.
 Performance tracking & Supply Chain Management by 3rd Parties and through various complex global supply chains.
 Develop skills in New Process Development, Quality Systems & Support.
 
 Role 5 – Pharmaceutical Science – Worthing 
 
 Degree requirements: Biomedical, Engineering or Life Sciences

 Workplace Arrangements: Full Time Onsite

 Overview of the Department 
 The Production Support team plays a critical role in ensuring the safe, compliant, and efficient manufacture of pharmaceutical products. Working closely with Production, Quality, Engineering, and Supply Chain teams, the department provides technical support to manufacturing operations, drives continuous improvement initiatives, and ensures compliance with GMP and regulatory requirements.
 As an Industrial Placement student, you will gain hands-on experience supporting manufacturing processes and equipment, investigating operational challenges, and contributing to projects that improve performance, quality, and compliance. The role provides exposure to cross-functional working, problem-solving methodologies, quality systems, and operational excellence within a highly regulated pharmaceutical environment.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 Provide troubleshooting support for production processes and equipment. Support process and technical investigations, including corrective and preventative actions and internal problem notifications.
 Supporting and in some cases owning key compliance processes and activities aligned to the value stream, including but not limited to, Self Inspections, deviation management, safety sampling, Risk Management (Local and RMS), Laboratory Investigation / Plant Investigations, CAPA, Customer and Vendor complaints, and planned change.
 Identify opportunities to improve the production process through robust problem solving and continuous improvement, tracking and ensuring beneficial delivery of corrective actions, preventative actions and minor projects for department against measurable targets
 Support inspection readiness and manage Audit activities across the aligned department.
 Support updates and maintenance of key documentation in the production areas. Assist with the review, update, and maintenance of production documentation, procedures, and technical records.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive operational, quality, and business objectives.
 Develop an understanding of pharmaceutical manufacturing, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence principles.
 
 Role 6 - Business and Supply Chain - Montrose 
 
 Degree requirements: Logistics, Manufacturing, Supply Chain

 Workplace Arrangements: Full time on site required

 Overview of the Department 
 The Scheduling Department at Montrose plays a critical role in ensuring the seamless coordination of production timelines across various functions. This team is responsible for managing schedules that align with supply chain demands, regulatory requirements, and operational capacity to meet business objectives. Their work helps optimize workflows, minimize delays, and maintain a consistent supply of products to patients and customers worldwide.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 Production plan scheduling for pharmaceutical manufacturing.
 Day to day supporting the business with takings actions, problem solving and collaborating with support functions.
 Support and carry out continuous improvement projects.
 Contributing to the wider site Smart Manufacturing initiatives, investigating opportunities for digital solutions. 
 Engage in warehouse inbound and outbound activities.
 
 Role 7 - Business and Supply Chain - Ware 
 
 Degree requirements: Open to any degree

 Workplace Arrangements: Full time onsite required

 Overview of the Department 
 The Ware manufacturing site is GSK’s flagship location for New Product Introduction (NPI) and plays a critical role in the delivery of life-changing medicines to patients worldwide. Interns in Supply & Logistics will be at the heart of this mission, supporting the seamless flow of materials and products across a complex global network.
 The Supply & Logistics department at the Ware manufacturing site is responsible for orchestrating end-to-end supply chain operations that ensure timely and efficient delivery of pharmaceutical products, which includes both oral solid dose (OSD) platforms and dry powder inhalers. The function comprises of Production & Materials Scheduling, Warehouse Operations, Harmonization team (Business & Data Process Experts), Launch & Data and Product Lifecycle Management. In this role you will have the opportunity to get involved in work across the entire Logistics function to support and manage the delivery of key improvement projects, such as improving Warehouse capacity and material availability, advanced scheduling programmes and lead time reduction.
 Key Placement Learnings 
 Drive continuous improvement initiatives across Supply & Logistics, identifying opportunities to streamline processes and reduce waste.
 Utilize GSK continuous improvement methodologies to drive change and solve top problems.
 Support Warehouse Operations to deliver key objectives such as Warehouse capacity improvement.
 Support both the Launch & Data and the Harmonization Teams to improve data delivery.
 Assist with digital transformation by developing and implementing solutions using Power BI, Power Apps, and other SMART Manufacturing technologies.
 
 Apply now! 

 These placement opportunities have the following recruitment stages – you must successfully pass each stage to be offered a placement year with GSK for 2027:

 1. Complete Connectr activity – obtain your personal code - please follow this link to complete
 2. Eligibility Form – enter your personal code
 3. GSK Digital Assessment
 4. Some technical roles may require a short technical assessment
 5. Virtual Assessment Centre or Virtual Interview

 Note: Your Connectr application code is unique and must not be shared. Using someone else's code, or sharing your own, may result in your application being withdrawn.

 You can find hints and tips on our recruitment process and get guidance from real GSK mentors on our Early Careers Hub here .

 We’re 100% open to all talent. We want to recruit the right people for GSK from the widest possible backgrounds, so we can better serve the inclusion of our patients and because it’s the right thing to do. You can learn more about Inclusion at GSK here .

 For more information about GSK and our careers please visit our website here .

 Need help with your application? Please email us at UK.InternRecruitment@gsk.com or call us on 01582 692870 and let us know how we can help you.
 
 #Internships #UKEarlyCareers #GSKIndustrialPlacements #GSKEngineeringPlacements #GSKSciencePlacements #GSKGlobalSupplyChainPlacements #GSKSTEMPlacements #GSKLondon #GSKWare #GSKWorthing #GSKBarnardCastle #GSKNorthEast #GSKMontrose #GSKScotland

 Skills 
Audit Preparations, Business Continuity Management (BCM), Contractor Oversight, Data Integrity, Digital Fluency, Financial Acumen, GxP Regulations, Lean Management, Operational Execution, Problem Solving, Process Optimization, Risk Awareness, Scenario Planning, Supplier Relationship Management, Supply Chain Optimization, Troubleshooting 
 
 
 Why GSK?
Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. 
 
 GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.
 
 People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.
 
 GSK is an Equal Opportunity Employer. This ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), military service or any basis prohibited under federal, state or local law.
 
 We believe in an agile working culture for all our roles. If flexibility is important to you, we encourage you to explore with our hiring team what the opportunities are.
 
 Please don’t hesitate to contact us if you’d like to discuss any reasonable adjustments to our process which might help you demonstrate your strengths and capabilities.
 
 For UK Intern roles (including Industrial Placements) you can either call us on 01582 692870, or send an email uk.InternRecruitment@gsk.com 
 For UK Apprentice and Graduate Programme roles you can either call us on 0203 862 2277, or send an email uk.EarlyCareers@gsk.com 
 
 Important notice to Employment businesses/ Agencies 
 GSK does not accept referrals from employment businesses and/or employment agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site. All employment businesses/agencies are required to contact GSK's commercial and general procurement/human resources department to obtain prior written authorization before referring any candidates to GSK. The obtaining of prior written authorization is a condition precedent to any agreement (verbal or written) between the employment business/ agency and GSK. In the absence of such written authorization being obtained any actions undertaken by the employment business/agency shall be deemed to have been performed without the consent or contractual agreement of GSK. GSK shall therefore not be liable for any fees arising from such actions or any fees arising from any referrals by employment businesses/agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site.
 
 Please note that if you are a US Licensed Healthcare Professional or Healthcare Professional as defined by the laws of the state issuing your license, GSK may be required to capture and report expenses GSK incurs, on your behalf, in the event you are afforded an interview for employment. This capture of applicable transfers of value is necessary to ensure GSK’s compliance to all federal and state US Transparency requirements. For more information, please visit the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) website at https://openpaymentsdata.cms.gov/

86dec8ad07a4.description:
Hardware Engineering Internship 2027 

 Cambridge, UK | Full-time | Fixed-term, 10–12 weeks | Hybrid

 Salary: £30,000–£35,000 per annum, depending on experience, paid pro rata for the internship duration.

 About us 

 Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion. 

 Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.  

 About the role 

 Our full-time summer internships give current students in technical fields the opportunity to apply their skills and expertise in an industrial setting. 

 You will join us at our head office in Cambridge, UK, for 10 to 12 weeks, working alongside talented software and hardware engineers, mathematicians, quantum information theorists and physicists who are experts in their fields. 

 You will have a dedicated supervisor and work on a project designed to make the best use of your existing skills while developing your knowledge of quantum computing and quantum error correction. We will support you in producing a meaningful piece of work that you can be proud of by the end of your internship. 

 Previous interns have committed code to industry-standard open-source compilers, co-authored research papers and led the design of new software tools. 

 What you will do 

 
 Collaborate with experienced hardware and software engineers to investigate and evaluate architectural optimisations 

 
 
 Enhance the decoder’s architecture to improve its flexibility and processing speed 

 
 
 Explore different design approaches and evaluate their potential benefits 

 
 
 Contribute to design decisions involving space and time trade-offs, balancing functionality, resource use and performance 

 
 
 Communicate your work clearly through technical discussions, presentations and written documentation 

 
 
 Develop your understanding of FPGA development, quantum computing and quantum error correction 

 
 What we need 

 
 You must be a current student at the time of application, either: 
 
 In the second or a later year of a Bachelor’s degree 

 Partway through a Master’s degree 

 Partway through a PhD 

 


 
 
 You must be studying Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, Physics, Mathematics or another related technical subject 

 
 
 Proficiency in Python 

 
 
 A solid understanding of low-level computer architecture 

 
 
 Excellent critical-thinking and problem-solving skills 

 
 
 Strong written and verbal communication skills 

 
 
 The ability to take initiative and work effectively as part of a team 

 
 
 A willingness to learn about FPGA development, quantum computing and quantum error correction 

 
 
 Availability to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks 

 
 Even better if… 

 
 You have experience with RTL development for FPGA or ASIC systems 

 
 
 You are familiar or interested in quantum computing 

 
 
 You understand optimisation concepts and performance trade-offs 

 
 
 You have some knowledge of networking principles 

 
 
 You have experience using version control, testing or debugging tools 

 
 Important notes 

 
 
 You must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the internship. If you hold a UK student visa, please check that its conditions allow you to undertake this full-time internship.



 
 
 PhD students may need to temporarily step away from their PhD to complete the internship. This may affect their right-to-work status, and applicants should check their individual circumstances 

 
 
 You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks during the summer vacation period 

 
 
 You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of any intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane 

 Internships are based at our head office in Cambridge, UK 

 
 How to apply 

 Please upload a CV and covering letter here. Your CV should include the grades that you have so far received in your degree(s). The covering letter should explain why you are applying for the internship and what skills and experience you can bring to the role. 

 Deadline 

 Please submit your application by Friday 6th November. Interviews will be held in Cambridge (or virtually if required). 

 What can you expect from us 

 Alongside a competitive salary, we offer private medical insurance, a health cash plan and life assurance, as well many other benefits. 

 You can also expect a diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 25 different nationalities. 

 If you have any queries, please contact jobs@riverlane. com . Please do not send your applications to this email address, all applications should be submitted via our careers page. 

 Everyone is welcome at Riverlane. We are an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from eligible and suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender reassignment, religion or belief, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, or pregnancy and maternity/paternity.

Cambridge, UK | Full-time | Fixed-term, 10–12 weeks | Hybrid

 Salary: £30,000–£35,000 per annum, depending on experience, paid pro rata for the internship duration.

 About us 

 Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion. 

 Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.  

 About the role 

 As a Research Intern at Riverlane, you will work on a focused project contributing to our quantum error correction research. Depending on the project, you could investigate error correction methods, develop and evaluate decoding algorithms, build simulations or explore the theoretical foundations of QEC. 

 You will work alongside researchers, mathematicians and engineers who are experts in their fields. You will have a dedicated supervisor who will help you shape your project, develop your knowledge and work towards a meaningful research outcome over your 10–12-week internship. This could include an analysis of a new approach, a mathematical model, a simulation or an algorithm. 

 We welcome students from a range of technical disciplines. You do not need extensive prior knowledge of quantum computing; we are looking for strong analytical skills, curiosity and a willingness to learn. 

 What you will do 

 
 Contribute to a focused research project aligned with Riverlane’s scientific goals. 

 
 
 Investigate theoretical or computational problems relating to quantum error correction. 

 
 
 Develop mathematical models, algorithms or simulations appropriate to your project. 

 
 
 Analyse results, compare approaches and draw evidence-based conclusions. 

 
 
 Collaborate with researchers and engineers, discussing ideas and learning from their expertise. 

 
 
 Communicate your findings through technical discussions, presentations and written reports. 

 
 
 Develop your understanding of quantum computing, QEC and the challenges of putting research into practice. 

 
 What we need 

 

 
 
 You must be a current student at the time of application, studying towards a Bachelor’s degree (second year or later), Master’s degree or PhD.



 
 You must be studying Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Electronic Engineering or another related technical subject.



 
 Evidence of strong theoretical, mathematical or computational skills, demonstrated through coursework, projects or research.



 
 Experience using at least one programming language.



 
 Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills.



 
 The ability to understand and work with complex technical concepts.



 
 Clear written and verbal communication skills.



 
 The ability to take initiative and work effectively as part of a team.



 
 An interest in quantum computing; extensive prior knowledge or experience is not required.



 
 Availability to work full-time for 10–12 weeks.



 
 

 Even better if… 

 
 You have experience with Python or another language commonly used for scientific computing 

 
 
 You have completed an independent research project or communicated technical research through a report, presentation or publication 

 
 
 You have experience using version control or collaborative software-development tools 

 
 Important notes 

 

 
 You must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the internship. If you hold a UK student visa, please check that its conditions allow you to undertake this full-time internship.

 
 

 
 PhD students may need to temporarily step away from their PhD to complete the internship. This may affect their right-to-work status, and applicants should check their individual circumstances 

 
 
 You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks during the summer vacation period 

 
 
 You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of any intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane 

 
 
 Internships are based at our head office in Cambridge, UK 

 
 

 

 How to apply 

 Please upload a CV and covering letter through our careers page. Your CV should include the grades you have received so far in your degree(s). Your covering letter should explain why you are applying for the research internship and what skills and experience you would bring.

 Deadline 

 Please submit your application by Friday 6 November 2026 . Interviews will be held in Cambridge, or virtually if required. 

   

 

 What can you expect from us 

 Alongside a competitive salary, we offer private medical insurance, a health cash plan and life assurance, as well many other benefits. 

 You can also expect a diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 25 different nationalities. 

 If you have any queries, please contact jobs@riverlane. com . Please do not send your applications to this email address, all applications should be submitted via our careers page. 

 Everyone is welcome at Riverlane. We are an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from eligible and suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender reassignment, religion or belief, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, or pregnancy and maternity/paternity. 

 Women and other underrepresented groups may be less likely to apply for a role unless they meet all or nearly all of the requirements. If this applies to you, we still encourage you to apply - you may be a great fit, even if you don’t meet every single qualification. We’d love to hear from you. 

 If you need any adjustments made to the application or selection process so you can do your best, please let us know. We will be happy to help.

 We have several different types of roles in different teams: 
 
 On Wing Technology (Bristol) - developing intuitive, responsive user interfaces for aerospace applications using modern web technologies. You will design and implement user-facing features with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, working closely with UI/UX designers to turn wireframes into high-quality code and ensure designs are technically feasible. The role involves collaborating with back-end developers to integrate front-end components, participating in agile practices (sprint planning, reviews, retrospectives), engaging in code reviews and best practices, troubleshooting and resolving issues, and staying current with emerging software development trends and technologies. 
 
 Software Engineering (Cheltenham) - use good engineering practice and AI tools to improve project outcomes across Quality, Delivery, and Cost: You strengthen code quality by following agreed coding standards, actively participating in code reviews, and suggesting maintainability improvements that help reduce long-term cost. You contribute to continuous improvement by engaging in team retrospectives and capturing changes that lower defects and delays, improving both Quality and Delivery. You build systems thinking by joining cross-team projects, learning how upstream and downstream changes affect Delivery, Quality, and Cost. You explore and share advances in tools, frameworks, and AI for engineering, focusing on options that improve Quality, accelerate Delivery, and reduce Cost. You use AI-assisted tools to generate and refine test ideas and documentation, validating outputs to improve Quality while reducing Cost and effort. You also apply AI to summarise technical articles and documentation for the team, helping spread knowledge quickly and efficiently, supporting Quality and Delivery at low Cost. 
 
 Software Tools (Cheltenham) - maintains, supports, and improves the engineering toolchains used across NPI projects. You will be supported by experienced engineers and a strong learning and continuous improvement culture as you learn the toolchains, contribute to support and enhancement work, and develop through hands-on projects, mentorship, and training. Key responsibilities include optimising day-to-day use of engineering tools (issue triage, root cause analysis, resolution), implementing and testing enhancements to improve usability, reliability, and performance, and translating stakeholder requests into requirements, design changes, implementation, and verification. You will document configurations, changes, known issues, and test evidence according to engineering policies, prepare and present technical findings and status updates, participate in cross-functional initiatives and continuous improvement activities, and provide timely updates on risks, issues, and progress to support short-term planning and unblock delivery. 
 
 Test Systems (Cheltenham) - you will train up be safe in Lab and Production areas, learn full software development lifecycle processes and adhere to them. Track and deliver software releases on time & identify improvements to projects. 
 
 Engineering Operations Power portfolio (Cheltenham) - provide support across digital transformation activities, helping to drive automation, simplification, and optimisation of business processes. Working with the Business Change Manager, you will help run an effective operating rhythm by preparing reports and dashboards, managing digital reporting tools, dashboards, and web apps, and supporting the implementation of new digital tools. You will track and administer digital transformation projects and other improvement activities, document business data sources, and contribute to defining a future data analytics strategy for Engineering Operations. The role also involves engaging cross-functionally, facilitating process reviews and improvements, and building strong relationships across the organisation. 
 
 You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK. 
 
 This opportunity is offered in our Bristol (Bristol Robotic Services) and Cheltenham sites , during the process we will ask you to share your location and role preferences. 
 
 GE Aerospace, Bristol Robotic Services (BRS) is a small tightknit office located in Bristol, South West England. We are a team of ~50 talented, dedicated and hardworking employees who collaborate to solve very interesting challenges in the aerospace industry. Every day at BRS is unique; you will be presented with exciting technical problems to solve and be given the space to innovate bespoke solutions. Given the small size of the company, it is very clear to see the impact your work makes, so if you are someone who grabs opportunity with both hands, you will find your time here very rewarding. 
 
We are looking for high-energy, self-motivated individuals with the vision to help carry our business forward.  The work is academically rigorous, intellectually demanding, and requires exceptional problem-solving, communication, leadership and interpersonal skills. That being said, we are a very collaborative bunch so we don’t need you to be an expert in everything, we have experts here who will mentor and coach you into developing the skills you need. 
 
Our offices are in Bristol in the South West of England – an area fast becoming a major centre for robotics. The South West is a beautiful place to live, with good infrastructure, great universities and fabulous beaches not far away from the city of Bristol. Our offices are located a few minutes’ walk from Filton Abbey Wood Station and on a regular bus route. 
 
 With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy. 
 
 Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge. Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come. 
 
 At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential. 
 
 Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight. 
 
 This placement role is an intended pipeline to our Edison Engineering Development Programme (EEDP) based in Cheltenham. Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to securing a role prior to the end of their placement year. 
 
 Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above! 
 
 If you love technology and desire a career in Engineering, EEDP is for you. 
 
 Edison Engineers understand and apply engineering fundamentals in the business environment and design, analyse, and test the technology that continues to innovate how the world flies sustainably. Find out more here https://invent.ge/eedp 
 
 If you are passionate about Software Engineering, we would like to hear from you. 
 
 Qualifications/Requirements 
 
 Currently studying a Computer Science/ Web Development/ Artificial Intelligence/ Data Science/ Mathematics/ Human-Computer Interaction/ Graphic Design/ Embedded Software/ Software Engineering/ Electrical and Electronics Engineering or related Bachelor’s or integrated Master’s Degree 
 Passionate about Software Engineering 
 Programming experience in at least one of C#, Java, or Python, with willingness to work across more than one language 
 On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above 
 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement 
 
 Desired Characteristics 
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects 
 Organised & able to work towards deadlines 
 Inspired and curious to learn 
 Strong verbal and written communication skills 
 Able to take ownership for projects 
 Analytical and problem-solving skills 
 Proficient in Microsoft Office 
 Able to work as part of a team 
 
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact. 
 
 Total Reward 
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible. 
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs. 
   
 Non-contributory Pension 
 Life Assurance 
 Group income protection  
 Private medical cover 
 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell 
 
 Recruitment Process 
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com . 
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. 
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too. 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS . 
 
 Right to Work 
 
 Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. 
 
 Further, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website. 
 
 Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward. 
 
 
 Additional Information 
 Relocation Assistance Provided: No
