Choose Wisely, Apply Confidently 
 To maximise your opportunities at securing an Industrial Placement with us this year, we strongly advise that you apply to no more than 3 adverts . (For clarity, multiple roles within a single advert are considered one application.)

 We encourage you to concentrate your efforts on the roles that best align with your skills, interests and university experience, as this will strengthen your application and give you the best chance of success.

 Roles Available in Locations : GSK HQ London

 Education required : See individual roles for degree requirements

 Please read the degree requirements for each role carefully before applying. 

 Other requirements : You will have completed a minimum of 2 years of your undergraduate degree but will not have graduated at the start of your placement. You must be enrolled at a UK (United Kingdom) or ROI (Republic of Ireland) University for the duration of your placement.

 Pre-application activity : Before applying, you'll need to obtain an application code by completing a short activity in Connectr, our candidate engagement platform.

 This activity is designed to encourage considered applications. Once completed, you'll receive your unique application code required to proceed with your application.

 If you have already graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree and are currently studying a postgraduate Masters, you are not eligible for this programme. 

 Language requirement : Written and spoken fluency in English

 Expected Start date : September 2027

 Duration : 1 year (approximately)

 Salary : A salary of £28,900 (London) plus a bonus.

 Workplace Arrangements: Flexible working via performance with choice (office & home working may be available)

 Application Closing : Roles are expected to close on 22/10/2026 , however, candidates will be reviewed regularly, and the advert may close at any point. Please ensure you review and complete the application stages below. 

 Are you looking to gain valuable real world work experience and help positively impact the lives of others? 

 A GSK internship offers you the opportunity to kickstart your career – to take on a real role with genuine impact. You’ll take on challenging tasks within live projects or assignments. You’ll also get to learn from others in your team and other parts of GSK whilst developing your skills and gaining valuable experience for wherever the future takes you.

 What do we offer you? 
 A competitive salary, with an annual bonus based on company performance.
 Employee recognition programs, which reward exceptional achievements.
 Access to our cutting-edge wellbeing platform: personalise your experience, help reduce stress, increase focus, build connections and resilience. You will also have access to a confidential helpline 24/7, mindfulness, health screenings and financial wellbeing support. 
 Access to Private Healthcare Insurance, including 24-hour access to an online GP.
 Optional Support: Includes identity protection, long-term care insurance, home, auto, and pet insurance
 Opportunities to work with Employee Resource Groups, providing opportunities to network, gain mentorship, and develop personally and professionally.
 Access to IPUnite which is a community of Early Careers programme participants offering development, networking and social connections to help you make the best of your programme. You will also be invited to join LinkedIn groups and pre-joining webinars, to enable you to connect and network with new students.
 2 volunteering days per year
 
 Typical skills you can expect to learn on this placement will include:
 Teamworking through working with multidisciplinary teams
 Communication (written & verbal)
 Time management
 Problem-solving
 Networking
 Data analysis and management
 Technical skills (detailed within each role description)
 
 The Roles (3 available) 

 This advert contains multiple roles. Please read each role carefully before proceeding as you will be asked to provide a preference later in the application process. 

 Role 1 – Biostatistics & Data Science - GSK HQ London 

 Degree requirements: Mathematics / Statistics / Data Sciences BSc

 Overview of the Department 

 Respiratory, Immunology and Inflammation (RII) Biostatistics is part of the RII Research Unit (RIIRU), a department focused on developing innovative medicines for respiratory, immune and inflammatory diseases. RII statisticians play a key role throughout the research and development of the drug pipeline, working closely with scientists, clinicians in areas such as medicine discovery, clinical trial design and statistical analysis. We provide statistical expertise in the design of studies and clinical trials (e.g. sample size determination and randomisation strategies), as well as the performing analysis and providing interpretation of data. 

 Key Placement Activities 
 Support professional statisticians in the design of studies and clinical trials (e.g. sample size determination and randomisation).
 Work with professional statisticians in preparing statistical analysis plans, model development, output QC, and the communication of results.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g. scientists, clinicians).
 Develop statistical programming skills in R and other software.
 Develop an understanding of statistical methods used throughout drug development.
 Learn and apply statistical methods through project work and internal training on advanced topics e.g. Quantitative Decision Making, Bayesian Dynamic Borrowing, Dose Response Modelling, etc.
 
 Role 2 - Clinical Programming and Business Excellence - GSK HQ London 

 Degree requirements - Preferably Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a Science/Technology related discipline.

 Overview of the Department 
 Clinical Programming play a critical role within the Biostatistics department. We support clinical research teams by performing programming and validation of datasets and outputs for the analysis and reporting of clinical trial data. Meanwhile ensuring data quality, accuracy and adherence to data standards and regulatory requirements. Clinical Programming collaborate closely with cross-functional teams such as Statistics, Data Management and Clinical teams to ensure data is fit for purpose and meets requirements for study analysis and reporting. This placement year will provide you with exposure to industry-standard tools, methodologies, and regulatory requirements while contributing to the advancement of life-changing therapies. You will gain an insight into cutting-edge clinical research and the development processes, with the opportunity to learn from and network with experienced professionals within GSK.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 Collaborate with statisticians and fellow professional programmers as part of a study team to develop datasets, tables, listings and figures to aid clinical trial reporting.
 Participate in programming activities for clinical trial reporting using SAS and/or R programming languages, whilst adhering to data standards and regulatory requirements.
 Conduct quality control checks on clinical trial data and outputs, identifying and resolving discrepancies or issues where possible and flagging data issues to necessary stakeholders.
 Assist in the preparation of standard documentation, including dataset specifications and reviewer guides.
 Opportunities to be involved in and contribute to other non-project initiatives within GSK, contributing towards development of the Biostatistics department.
 
 Role 3 - Quantitative Sciences Innovation – GSK HQ London 
 Degree requirements - Mathematics, Statistics, Data Sciences

 Overview of the Department 
 This is an exciting opportunity to join GSK and gain exposure for innovation in the field of Statistics and Data Science to help transform the way in which we use data and quantitative thinking to drive decision-making in R&D. We are growing our cutting-edge statistical innovation and data science capabilities by expanding the Quantitative Sciences Innovation (QSI) group led by Nicky Best. QSI is a methodologically focused, solution-oriented functional group within GSK’s Biostatistics department.

 Key Placement Learnings 
 Collaborate with your team to develop and explore novel methods for handling prediction problems
 Gain hands on coding experience developing Machine Learning and prediction modelling pipelines
 Understand the background and statistical methods important for drug development
 Provide analysis, reporting and interpretation of modelling projects
 Work in close consultation with professional methodologists and scientists working in medicine and vaccine development
 Become proficient in R programming and Python. Leverage version control through GitHub to enable collaboration
 Develop new skills working in an ‘agile’ way delivering on projects over short ‘sprints’
 Learn the theory of new statistical and machine learning methodologies and how to apply it by collaborating with highly skilled statisticians and attending training courses
 Experience the role of a statistical consultant, working closely with cross-functional teams to translate scientific or clinical problems into statistical ones
 Gain industry knowledge in potentially a wide range of therapeutic areas, overseeing short-term or long-term projects that cover multiple GSK drugs
 
 Apply now! 

 These placement opportunities have the following recruitment stages – you must successfully pass each stage to be offered a placement year with GSK for 2027:

1. Complete Connectr activity – obtain your personal code - please follow this link to complete
 2. Eligibility Form – enter your personal code
 3. GSK Digital Assessment
 4. Some technical roles may require a short technical assessment
 5. Virtual Assessment Centre or Virtual Interview

 Note : Your Connectr application code is unique and must not be shared. Using someone else's code, or sharing your own, may result in your application being withdrawn.

 You can find hints and tips on our recruitment process and get guidance from real GSK mentors on our Early Careers Hub here .

 We’re 100% open to all talent. We want to recruit the right people for GSK from the widest possible backgrounds, so we can better serve the inclusion of our patients and because it’s the right thing to do. You can learn more about Inclusion at GSK here .

 For more information about GSK and our careers please visit our website here .

 Need help with your application? Please email us at UK.InternRecruitment@gsk.com or call us on 01582 692870 and let us know how we can help you.

 #Internships #UKEarlyCareers #GSKIndustrialPlacements #GSKResearch&Development #GSKSTEMPlacements #GSKLondon

 Skills 
Applied Statistics, Data Analysis, Data Engineering, Data Science, Datasets, Drug Development, Drug Discovery Process, Drug Target Identification, Genetic Analysis, Genomic Analysis, Machine Learning (ML), Software Engineering 
 
 
 Why GSK?
Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. 
 
 GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.
 
 People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.
 
 GSK is an Equal Opportunity Employer. This ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), military service or any basis prohibited under federal, state or local law.
 
 We believe in an agile working culture for all our roles. If flexibility is important to you, we encourage you to explore with our hiring team what the opportunities are.
 
 Please don’t hesitate to contact us if you’d like to discuss any reasonable adjustments to our process which might help you demonstrate your strengths and capabilities.
 
 For UK Intern roles (including Industrial Placements) you can either call us on 01582 692870, or send an email uk.InternRecruitment@gsk.com 
 For UK Apprentice and Graduate Programme roles you can either call us on 0203 862 2277, or send an email uk.EarlyCareers@gsk.com 
 
 Important notice to Employment businesses/ Agencies 
 GSK does not accept referrals from employment businesses and/or employment agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site. All employment businesses/agencies are required to contact GSK's commercial and general procurement/human resources department to obtain prior written authorization before referring any candidates to GSK. The obtaining of prior written authorization is a condition precedent to any agreement (verbal or written) between the employment business/ agency and GSK. In the absence of such written authorization being obtained any actions undertaken by the employment business/agency shall be deemed to have been performed without the consent or contractual agreement of GSK. GSK shall therefore not be liable for any fees arising from such actions or any fees arising from any referrals by employment businesses/agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site.
 
 Please note that if you are a US Licensed Healthcare Professional or Healthcare Professional as defined by the laws of the state issuing your license, GSK may be required to capture and report expenses GSK incurs, on your behalf, in the event you are afforded an interview for employment. This capture of applicable transfers of value is necessary to ensure GSK’s compliance to all federal and state US Transparency requirements. For more information, please visit the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) website at https://openpaymentsdata.cms.gov/

About the Role 
 The AI Solutions Intern will support the development and deployment of practical agentic AI and automation solutions across Bosch Central Sales. Working with business, sales, engineering and enabling-function teams, the role will translate clearly defined business problems into usable solutions that deliver measurable benefits.
 The successful candidate will take ideas from initial discovery through rapid proof of concept, user testing, controlled deployment and adoption. They will work within Bosch-approved technologies, information-security requirements and responsible AI principles, with appropriate technical and business oversight.
 This is a delivery-focused internship offering practical experience in AI solution development, process improvement, stakeholder engagement and change adoption within the Central Sales organisation.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Solution Development & Deployment 
 Rapidly develop working proofs of concept using Bosch-approved AI, automation and data technologies in response to prioritised Central Sales business problems.
 Work with process owners and subject-matter experts to define requirements, success measures, data needs and expected business benefits.
 Extend successful proofs of concept into robust working solutions that can be adopted across Central Sales and, where appropriate, the wider Bosch UK organisation.
 Test solutions with users, capture feedback and refine functionality, usability and reliability before deployment.
 Measure and communicate outcomes such as time saved, improved quality, reduced manual effort, faster decision-making or improved customer support.
 Stakeholder Engagement & Adoption 
 Engage Central Sales stakeholders across business and engineering functions to identify, assess and prioritise suitable AI use cases.
 Create clear communications that explain the business problem, the proposed solution, expected benefits and any changes required from users.
 Produce practical user guidance and training content to support solution rollout and adoption across the Central Sales team.
 Support demonstrations, training sessions, workshops and knowledge-sharing activities across Central Sales and the wider Bosch UK network.
 Documentation, Governance & Support 
 Document solution objectives, workflows, data inputs, operating instructions, ownership and support arrangements.
 Apply Bosch requirements for information security, data protection, responsible AI and solution governance throughout development and deployment.
 Engage the user community after launch, monitor utilisation and identify opportunities to improve or scale solutions.
 AI Capability Development 
 Develop knowledge of emerging AI technologies and assess their practical relevance to Central Sales processes and customer-facing activities.
 Share reusable approaches, lessons learned and good practice with colleagues and relevant Bosch UK communities.
 Contribute to a Central Sales pipeline of AI opportunities and support prioritisation based on value, feasibility, risk and scalability.
 Essential 
 Currently studying towards a degree in a quantitative subject for example Computer Science, Data Science, Software Engineering, Engineering, Mathematics or a related discipline.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Demonstrable interest in artificial intelligence, automation and emerging technologies.
 Experience of programming, automation or data analysis gained through university, placements or personal projects.
 Good communication, presentation and stakeholder-engagement skills.
 Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across multiple teams.
 Desirable personal Attributes 

The ideal candidate will be:
 Curious, proactive and eager to learn.
 Able to simplify code.
 This is a 12-month internship beginning in July 2027. This position is open to undergraduate students who are eligible to partake in a work placement as part of their university course. 
 Location: you will be based at the Coventry office. 
 As an Intern at Bosch, you will participate in an exclusive learning and development programme called the BUILD Programme designed to support you through your internship journey. It includes a mixture of in-person and virtual sessions on topics including Effective Communication and Leading Myself provided by expert external trainers.
 Interview Process and Right to Work Information: 
 Shortlisted candidates will then be invited to participate in a face-to-face interview by the hiring team and/or an online assessment centre.
 You must have the right to live and work in the UK when you start your placement and for the full duration of your placement. Please note your placement must be directly relevant to your course to comply with visa requirements.
 Before attending an interview for this position you must inform your Faculty/School Placement Officer and we strongly suggest you check you are eligible for a placement before you apply. If your Faculty/School does not have a Placement Officer, you must inform your course tutor.

 Company: 
Boeing United Kingdom Limited 
 
 The Boeing Global Technology team based at the Boeing Aerospace Innovation Centre (AIC) in Prestwick, Scotland, are looking for highly motivated individuals to join our team for a three-month summer internship in 2027. Our team of around 60 people at the AIC work on innovative, cutting-edge technology development, from robotics and automation, to composite fabrication, and digital engineering. Our team of multi skilled engineers work together in our 100,000ft2 state of the art research facility at Prestwick International Airport in the West coast of Scotland, to develop manufacturing technologies that will help to build the next generation of aircraft.

 As a Research and Technology (R&T) intern you will be given a real-life industrial challenge to solve over the course of a three-month placement. Working on your own, or as part of a small team, you will be given the tools and support from a highly skilled R&T team to develop a solution that is both innovative and cost effective. The project will be split between the office and the workshop as you plan, develop, and deliver a working solution.

 Understanding and defining requirements
 Budget and schedule planning
 Landscaping and down selecting solutions
 Design, develop, and validate solutions through small scale prototypes and test
 Building relationships with stakeholders and team members
 Reporting progress to key stakeholders and senior management
 Skills 
 Confident and clear communicator

 Keen interest in aerospace manufacturing processes and digital technologies

Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?

 About Analog Devices 
 Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X .

 At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network.

 ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees.

 At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles.

 Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.

 
 Software Engineering Intern – Electric Vehicle Battery Management System 
 Are you passionate about sustainable technology and excited to gain hands-on experience in electric vehicle software development? We're looking for a motivated Software Engineering Intern to join our team and contribute to the development of a cutting-edge web application for our advanced vehicle Battery Management System (BMS).
 This is an excellent opportunity to work alongside experienced engineers and gain practical experience developing software that helps optimize battery performance, longevity, and safety for the next generation of electric vehicles (EVs).
 About the Role 
 As a Software Engineering Intern, you will support the development and maintenance of a modern, interactive, and secure web application that visualizes real-time and historical battery data. You'll collaborate with experienced software engineers while learning industry best practices in web development, testing, and deployment.
 Location: Edinburgh, Scotland 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Contribute to the development and enhancement of the BMS application under the guidance of senior engineers. 
 Develop and maintain responsive user interfaces using React to display battery data, dashboards, and diagnostic information. 
 Assist with the development of APIs and backend services that process data from vehicle telematics systems. 
 Support software quality initiatives by creating and maintaining unit, integration, and end-to-end tests. 
 Collaborate with embedded, application, and web software engineers to understand requirements and implement features. 
 Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and agile development activities. 
 Help investigate and resolve software defects and performance issues. 
 What You'll Bring (Required Skills) 
 Currently pursuing, or recently completed, a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
 Experience with software development through academic projects, internships, personal projects, or open-source contributions. 
 Familiarity with JavaScript/TypeScript and modern web development concepts. 
 Familiarity with REST APIs and web services. 
 Basic experience with React. 
 Understanding of software testing principles and version control systems such as Git. 
 Strong problem-solving skills and enthusiasm for learning new technologies. 
 Excellent communication and teamwork skills. 
 Bonus Points (Nice-to-Have) 
 Experience with Node.js or backend web development. 
 Interest in electric vehicles, battery technology, automotive systems, or IoT applications. 
 Experience building data visualization dashboards or working with charting libraries. 
 Knowledge of CI/CD concepts and automated testing tools. 
 Basic understanding of electronics, embedded systems, or vehicle technologies. 
 What You'll Gain 
 Mentorship from experienced software and systems engineers. 
 Hands-on experience working on production software in the electric vehicle industry. 
 Exposure to modern web technologies, development practices, and testing frameworks. 
 Experience collaborating in a multidisciplinary engineering team.

Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?

 About Analog Devices 
 Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X .

 At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network.

 ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees.

 At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles.

 Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.

 Locations: Edinburgh, Glasgow, Newbury, London 

 Are you looking to work for a company that is a leader in technology that makes the world smarter, safer, healthier and greener? If so, then Analog Devices International is the destination for you 
 


 Leading Edge Technology; From digital healthcare to 5G connectivity, from autonomous and electric vehicles to the digitised factory, Analog Devices is passionate about turning tomorrow's possibilities into reality, making the world smarter, safer, healthier and greener. Wherever digital meets physical we’re there. Virtually every wireless call, text, and download today passes through an Analog Devices IC. Our automotive battery monitoring technology is used in the majority of petrol and diesel engine cars with engine start-stop functionality. This helped prevent 33 million metric tons of carbon vehicle emissions last year globally, which is more than half of all the carbon emissions the whole of Ireland produces in a single year. In digital x-ray imaging our technology enables delivery of increasingly high image fidelity at lower radiation dosages. Because we are dedicated to solving the toughest engineering challenges, Analog Devices is one of the top 10 semiconductor companies in the world. 

 
 We don’t just talk about innovation, we live it ; At ADI, we believe that work should be exciting and meaningful. We encourage initiative and creativity, and we actively support the free exchange of ideas. A career with ADI means taking part in innovation and being challenged to achieve, and it offers the opportunity to work with other talented people, using state-of-the art processes and equipment. We run an annual Innovation Award for our Interns, a Global Early Employee Challenge for recent grads, and Hackathons for our wider community of employees. At ADI we strive to be Ahead of What’s Possible .

 
 Silicon Meets Software; Software development at ADI spans from edge nodes to generating insights in the cloud – and everything in between. Working with hardware teams, your software skills in planning, systems architecture, designing, developing, troubleshooting, debugging, and testing can help to unlock the potential of our algorithms, technology platforms, and systems to make a real-world impact. Areas where our hardware and software technologies combine to offer real-world, system solutions include IoT smart building applications, automotive radar systems for autonomous driving and collision avoidance, vital signs monitoring in the healthcare space, and 5G communications infrastructure. As ADI continues to grow its software capability, we’re also focussed on building expertise in Machine Learning and AI. We’re looking to hire people who want to make science fiction real.

 

 One Company, Unlimited Opportunity; The scale of Analog Devices and the range of technologies we develop, markets we serve, countries we operate in, and skills that we utilise, makes for an exciting opportunity for you to find your direction.  What's the secret to our success? It's very simple –we treat our employees as our greatest asset.

Duration: 12 weeks 
 Salary: £2500 per month 
 Start date: June 2027 
 Application deadline: Midnight 29 th November 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 

 The Internship Programme at Graphcore 

 Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence. 

 What you’ll work on

 Bring your curiosity, bright ideas and problem-solving skills to the chips behind tomorrow’s AI systems.

 As a Silicon summer intern, you’ll join one of our four specialist Silicon teams: logical design, verification, physical design or design for test (DFT). You’ll contribute to real chip development, learning from experienced colleagues and building your understanding of how advanced AI chips are designed, verified and prepared for manufacture.

 Depending on your team, you’ll work on areas such as register-transfer level (RTL) design, SOC integration, verification methods, physical implementation or the critical role of DFT. You’ll use industry-standard electronic design automation (EDA) tools and take ownership of clear tasks, with support from experienced engineers.

 How you’ll learn and grow

 During the 12-week programme, you’ll develop practical silicon engineering skills in the team you join, building on the fundamentals you’ve learned through your studies and projects.

 Hands-on tasks will help you learn modern design techniques and use industry-standard EDA tools. You’ll build skills in areas such as RTL, verification, timing or physical design, depending on your team’s focus.

 Feedback from reviews and practical problem solving will help you develop your technical judgement, explain your approach and understand how your work fits into the wider chip development process. Bring your curiosity and willingness to learn; we’ll support you as you build your knowledge and confidence.

 What we're looking for

 
 Working towards a degree in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science, or a related subject such as Physics or Maths. 

 Technical skills in C, C++ or Python, demonstrated through study, projects, hobbies or practical experience 

 An interest in AI compute and silicon design, including ASICs, verification, logical design, DFT or physical design, with motivation to learn EDA tools and modern design techniques 

 A curious, self-starting approach, with examples from activities or hobbies beyond your studies, plus clear communication and the ability to work well with others 

 
 You don’t need an engineering background to join us. If you’re curious, motivated and enjoy solving problems, we’ll teach you the skills you need. 

 Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects, hobbies or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned. 

 Benefits 

 
 Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work 

 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship 

 Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista 

 Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform 

 
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. 

 We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you. 

 Sponsorship 

 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities. 

 Introduction to Graphcore 

 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacentre scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. 

 An internship at Graphcore gives you the chance to explore where your interests and skills could take you. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. Together, you’ll share ideas and solve challenging problems, building experience and confidence to help you decide what comes next. 

 How to apply and what to expect 

 To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring. 

 Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.

Choose Wisely, Apply Confidently 
 
 To maximise your opportunities at securing an Industrial Placement with us this year, we strongly advise that you apply to no more than 3 adverts . (For clarity, multiple roles within a single advert are considered one application.) 
 
 We encourage you to concentrate your efforts on the roles that best align with your skills, interests and university experience, as this will strengthen your application and give you the best chance of success. 
 
 Roles Available in Location : Montrose, Ware 
 
 Education required : To apply for this placement, you must be: 
 Currently studying an Undergraduate Degree in Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Pharmaceutical Science, Pharmacy or related 
 
 Please read the degree requirements for each role carefully before applying. 
 
 Other requirements : You will have completed a minimum of 2 years of your undergraduate degree but will not have graduated at the start of your placement. You must be enrolled at a UK (United Kingdom) or ROI (Republic of Ireland) University for the duration of your placement. 
 
 Pre-application activity : Before applying, you'll need to obtain an application code by completing a short activity in Connectr, our candidate engagement platform. 
 
 This activity is designed to encourage considered applications. Once completed, you'll receive your unique application code required to proceed with your application
 
 If you have already graduated with a bachelor’s degree and are currently studying a postgraduate Masters, you are not eligible for this programme. 
 
 Language requirement : Written and spoken fluency in English 
 
 Expected Start date : July 2027 
 
 Duration : 1 year (approximately) 
 
 Salary : A salary of £26,400 plus a bonus.

 Application Closing : Roles are expected to close on 22/10/26 , however, candidates will be reviewed regularly, and the advert may close at any point.

 Please ensure you review and complete the application stages below. 
 
 Are you looking to gain valuable real world work experience and help positively impact the lives of others? 
 
 A GSK internship offers you the opportunity to kickstart your career – to take on a real role with genuine impact. You’ll take on challenging tasks within live projects or assignments. You’ll also get to learn from others in your team and other parts of GSK whilst developing your skills and gaining valuable experience for wherever the future takes you. 
 
 What do we offer you? 
 
 A competitive salary, with an annual bonus based on company performance. 
 Employee recognition programs, which reward exceptional achievements. 
 Access to our cutting-edge wellbeing platform: personalise your experience, help reduce stress, increase focus, build connections and resilience. You will also have access to a confidential helpline 24/7, mindfulness, health screenings and financial wellbeing support. 
 Access to Private Healthcare Insurance, including 24-hour access to an online GP. 
 Optional Support: Includes identity protection, long-term care insurance, home, auto, and pet insurance 
 Opportunities to work with Employee Resource Groups, providing opportunities to network, gain mentorship, and develop personally and professionally. 
 Access to IPUnite which is a community of Early Careers programme participants offering development, networking and social connections to help you make the best of your programme. You will also be invited to join LinkedIn groups and pre-joining webinars, to enable you to connect and network with new students. 
 2 volunteering days per year 
 
 Typical skills you can expect to learn on this placement will include: 
 Teamworking through working with multidisciplinary teams 
 Communication (written & verbal) 
 Time management 
 Problem-solving 
 Networking 
 Data analysis and management 
 Technical skills (detailed within each role description) 
 
 The Roles (3 available) 
 
 This advert contains multiple roles. Please read each role carefully before proceeding as you will be asked to provide a preference in the application process. 
 
 Role 1 – Analytical Chemistry – Montrose 
 
 Degree requirements: Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry 
 
 Workplace Arrangements: Full time on site required 
 
 Overview of the Department 
 There is an opportunity at the Montrose site to join our Analytical Chemistry function within the Montrose Site MSAT group. The Manufacturing Science and Technology function (MSAT) group technical investigations and supports site manufacturing covering process chemistry, process engineering, organic chemistry and analytical sciences. 
 
 The role would suit an individual with a real passion for analytical science & instrumental analysis and key activities include bringing new processes to the site and the ongoing improvement of existing and established analytical methods already used at Montrose. 
 
 Key Placement Learnings 
 Build spectroscopic (IR/NMR/MS), chromatographic (HPLC/GC) and materials science (SEM/XRPD) analysis skills 
 Carrying out instrumental analysis to support the site's new process introductions and existing process improvement initiatives. 
 Resolve analytical issues that are disrupting the efficient operation of the operating units.                                                                                                                                     
 Spectroscopic characterisation of novel and unknown entities. 
 Gain an appreciation of the role of analytical science to the running of a pharmaceutical site including method validation & GMP.                                                                         
                                               
 Role 2: Synthetic Organic Chemistry – Montrose 
 
 Degree requirements: Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Synthetic Chemistry 
 
 Working Arrangements: Full time on site required 
 
 Overview of the Department 
 There is an opportunity at the Montrose site to join Synthetic Organic Chemistry function within the Montrose Site MSAT group. The Manufacturing Science and Technology group (MSAT) conducts technical investigations and supports site manufacturing covering process chemistry, process engineering, organic chemistry and analytical sciences. 
 
 The role would suit an individual with a real passion for practical synthetic organic chemistry and key activities would include bringing new processes to the site and the ongoing improvement of existing and established chemical processes already located at Montrose. 
 
 Key Placement Learnings 
 Carrying out organic synthesis experiments to support the site's new process introductions and existing process improvement initiatives. 
 Resolve organic chemistry issues that are disrupting the efficient operation of the operating units. 
 Isolating, characterising and synthesising novel impurities and chemical entities. 
 Develop strong practical laboratory organic synthesis using a range of classical and automated synthetic organic chemistry equipment. 
 Building spectroscopic characterisation skills. 
 
 
 Role 3: Materials Science – Ware 
 
 Degree requirements: Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Pharmaceutical Science, Pharmacy or related 
 
 Workplace Arrangements - Full time on site required 
 
 Overview of the Department 
 
 Materials Science is a division within Global Supply Chain Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT). We support products globally, both for GSK sites and externally. Whilst we work predominantly on small molecule medicines through lifecycle (both New Product Introduction – NPI, and established products), we also do some work on large molecule and vaccines products. We are a characterisation-focused team, getting involved with business-critical troubleshooting and investigations, proactive risk assessment for material changes e.g. API changes, as well as NPI milestones, and analytical method development, transfer and troubleshooting. 
 
 Key Placement Learnings 
 Leading and supporting characterisation-focused projects, including measurement, interpretation, reporting, and presentation of data across a range of physical property characterisation techniques for stakeholders across the business 
 Ensuring adherence to Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) 
 May be responsible for the procurement, qualification, calibration and maintenance of laboratory equipment 
 Accountability of key lab safety and compliance tasks, such as waste management, airflow and balance checks 
 Supporting key safety metrics and participating in departmental audits to maintain safety and operational standards 
 Leading and supporting Continuous Improvement (CI) activities, including sustainability-related tasks as part of initiatives to maintain a 'Green Lab' environment 
 
 Apply now! 
 
 These placement opportunities have the following recruitment stages – you must successfully pass each stage to be offered a placement year with GSK for 2027: 
 
 1. Complete Connectr activity – obtain your personal code - please follow this link to complete. 
 2. Eligibility Form – enter your personal code 
 3. GSK Digital Assessment 
 4.  Some technical roles may require a short technical assessment 
 5.  Virtual Assessment Centre or Virtual Interview 
 
 Note: Your Connectr application code is unique and must not be shared. Using someone else's code, or sharing your own, may result in your application being withdrawn.

 You can find hints and tips on our recruitment process and get guidance from real GSK mentors on our Early Careers Hub here . 
 
 We’re 100% open to all talent. We want to recruit the right people for GSK from the widest possible backgrounds, so we can better serve the inclusion of our patients and because it’s the right thing to do. You can learn more about Inclusion at GSK here . 
 
 For more information about GSK and our careers please visit our website here . 
 
 Need help with your application? Please email us at UK.InternRecruitment@gsk.com or call us on 01582 692870 and let us know how we can help you.

 Skills 
Analytical Chemistry, Analytical Instrumentation, Analytical Laboratory, Bioprocessing, Data Analysis Tools, Laboratory Reports 
 
 
 Why GSK?
Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. 
 
 GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

Job Description Summary 
Summary 

In the 12-month Digital Technology (DT) Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience, providing support in either business or technical areas of Information Technology. 
 
 Job Description 
 About GE Aerospace 
 
 Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft . You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives . Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world! 
 
 Digital Technology 
 
 Be a part of an exciting data transformation journey within GE Aerospace. On our Digital Technology team, you’ll have a hand in designing, deploying, and maintaining technologies and systems to address the ever-changing needs of our customers and business. 
 
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 
 In the 12-month placement in Digital Technology (DT) you’ll gain hands-on experience in IT operations, project management, data analytics, and software development. You’ll work on exciting projects to improve business processes, support IT systems, and drive digital transformation. 
 
 We have different types of roles in this area; here is a brief snapshot into each: 
 
 Digital Technolog y (Cardiff) - you will play a key part in developing a Digital Toolset to drive productivity within the business functions. You will lead various projects utilising applications from the GE Toolset and new Analytics Tools. You will partner with these business functions to understand requirements and translate these into Operational Tools. 
 
 Digital Technology (Caledonian) - Development of prototype local applications for SQDIP improvements. 
 
 DT Technology and Operations Team (Cheltenham) - providing support for iPhone and iPad devices, including setup, upgrades, compliance, and issue resolution. You will manage requests for new network port installations, remote access, and GUEST WiFi changes, while assisting users with supply chain applications. Responsibilities also include managing a Raspberry Pi-based signage solution, covering procurement, build, and configuration of devices. Project activities may involve supporting application deployments and upgrades, as well as managing small-scale equipment deployments and installations. 
 
 Digital Technology ( Dowty) - improving how the business uses data and digital technologies to drive better decisions and performance. You will help enhance data maturity by improving data quality, structure, standardization, governance, and accessibility, and work with business and digital teams to understand reporting needs and develop dashboards and visualizations for key metrics. The position involves gathering, cleaning, validating , and analyzing data to support operational and strategic decisions, while identifying opportunities where AI can create business value and building clear business cases for adoption. You will research digital and AI trends and best practices, help evaluate AI use cases for impact, feasibility, risks, and data readiness, and lead or coordinate a digital technology project from scope definition through milestone tracking and stakeholder communication. In addition, you will support cross-functional collaboration to ensure solutions align with user needs, prepare presentations and updates for reviews, and contribute to process improvements that enhance efficiency, visibility, and decision-making. 
 
 Cyber Security (Cheltenham) - you will work across five key cyber security areas: Intelligence, Enterprise Vulnerability Management, Insider Threat, External Threat, and Digital Forensics. The student will spend two months in each area, gaining an understanding of daily operations by working with key staff and delivering a small project to showcase what they have learned. In the final two months, the student can choose one of these areas to focus on. Throughout the placement, they will receive training and hands-on experience with cyber tools used by the UK Cyber Team, explore topics aligned to their course such as malware analysis and networking, and have opportunities to participate in Cyber Capture the Flag events during the year. 
 
 Engineering Leadership ( Cheletenham ) - data and digital - focused role embedded in engineering, closely linked to supply chain and factory operations. Reporting to the Engineering Executive Leader, you will support major initiatives such as Product Cost Hoshin Kanri , Defect PSR, and zero-defect improvement activities by using data analytics, digital tools, and AI/advanced analytics to analyse product cost and defect data, build dashboards and digital solutions, and drive lean, data-driven process and quality improvements. Key responsibilities include applying statistical and data science techniques to product cost data, creating visual dashboards (Tableau, Power BI, Excel), exploring AI methods (predictive models, clustering, anomaly detection), and collaborating with engineering, supply chain, IT/digital, and cross-functional teams. You will also develop defect analytics tools, use AI/ML for defect pattern recognition and risk scoring, participate in Genba at the factory to link digital insights to real processes, and help shape data pipelines, performance metrics, and visual management that support continuous improvement in Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost. 
 
 This placement is perfect for students who want to grow their skills and gain valuable expe rience in digital technology. 
 
 You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK. 
 
 This opportunity is offered in our Cardiff, Caledonian (Prestwick, Scotland) , Cheltenham and Gloucester (Dowty, a GE Aerospace company) sites , during the process we will ask you to share your location and role preferences. 
 
 GE Aerospace Wales specialises in the maintenance, repair and overhaul of a range of commercial jet engines. The facility, based in Nantgarw, just north of Cardiff, occupies over 1.2 million square feet of workshop space and has two state-of-the-art aircraft engine test facilities, along with a significant repair capability – known as Component Repair Wales. 
 
 The site has the capability to provide maintenance, repair and overhaul services for a range of engine types – including the world’s most powerful commercial aircraft engine the GE90-115B and the world’s most popular commercial engine the CFM56. 
 
 As one of the largest commercial aircraft engine maintenance facilities in the world, with annual sales of over $2bn, the business works with over 90 customers worldwide, including Emirates, TUI, Lufthansa, Delta, United, ANA and British Airways. 
 
 In 2017, the Wales site was selected as the Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility of choice for the GE9X; which will become the world’s largest and most fuel-efficient jet engine when it launches into service. The business will benefit from a £5m investment from the Welsh Government to support the total £20m investment put forward by the business, to equip and upskill the facility to be ready to maintain the GE9X fleet when it enters service on the new Boeing 777X aircraft. 
 
 The Wales team places a strong focus on providing career opportunities for talented individuals . Our apprenticeship, internship and work experience opportunities have been built to ensure the long-term success of our business by developing the next generation of technical, engineering and problem-solving talent. 
 
 GE Aerospace Caledonian is a purpose-built aircraft engine overhaul facility, adjacent to Glasgow Prestwick International Airport. The Caledonian site was officially opened in 1980 and has since grown into a centre of excellence for Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO) of CF6 & GEnx engine types. After each overhaul, the engines undergo intensive performance testing on site in our bespoke test cell, before returning to our global customer base ready for service. 
 
 Our vastly experienced and innovative workforce are passionate in the contribution towards the training of future engineers, leaders and surrounding talent in our organisation. At GE Caledonian, our Apprentices (Foundation, Modern & Graduate), XLP, OMLP and interns are key members of our team helping achieve the challenges of tomorrow. They continuously develop new skills to keep up with the pace of change in the Aviation Industry and become comfortable working in this ever-challenging environment which thrives on embracing change. 
 
 Our diverse team have a strong foothold in the local community, proactively seeking new volunteering opportunities to give back and deliver on our corporate responsibility. We have a dedicated affinity group on site who facilitate opportunities to the wider team, creating an inclusive culture we can all be proud of. 
 
 With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy.   
 
 Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge . Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come.   
 
 At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential.   
 
 Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight.   
 
 Dowty, a GE Aerospace company , is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for A wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft. 
 
 Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De-Haviland, Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J. 
 
 Operated by a highly skilled workforce, Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976; and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers. 
 
 This placement role is an intended pipeline for our Digital Technology Leadership Programme (DTLP) based in Cheltenham . Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to secure a role prior to the end of their placement year. 
 
 Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above! 
 
 If you are passionate about Digital Technology, we would love to hear from you. 
 
 Qualifications / Requirements 
 
 Currently studying an Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Information Management, IT Project Management, Cyber Security, ICT , Software Engineering, or Digital Technology Bachelor’s or integrated Master’s degree 

 Passionate about Digital Technology      

 On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above 

 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement 

 
 Desired Characteristics 
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects 

 Organised & able to work towards deadlines 

 Inspired and curious to learn 

 Strong verbal and written communication skills 

 Able to take ownership for projects 

 Analytical and problem-solving skills 

 Proficient in Microsoft Office 

 Able to work as part of a team 

 Working knowledge of full-stack development tools, SQL and Python 

 
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact. 
 
 Total Reward 
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice , gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible. 
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs. 
   
 Non-contributory Pension 

 Life Assurance 

 Group income protection 

 Private medical cover 

 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell 

 
 Recruitment Process 
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com.  
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31 st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. 
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too. 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS . 
 
 UK Security Clearance 
 
 UK Security Clearance (SC) may be required and maintained for some of our placement roles. Due to the nature of work, some of these roles are restricted to candidates who are a British National, or a dual National where one of the dual nationalities is British subject to any restrictions. Candidates who do not meet the minimum requirements for UK Security Clearance will therefore not be eligible for some of our roles on grounds of national security. If UK Security Clearance is not obtained for some roles, any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. 
 
 Right to Work 
 
 Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. 
 
 Further, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website. 
 
 Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward.

Location: Bristol, UK 
 Duration: 12 weeks 
 Salary: £2500 per month 
 Start date: June 2027 
 Application deadline: Midnight 29th November 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 

 The Internship Programme at Graphcore 

 Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence. 

 What you’ll work on 

 Put your low-level programming skills to work on the drivers that connect Graphcore’s AI hardware with machine learning software. 

 As a Software Engineering Intern in Drivers and Utilities, you’ll explore kernel and user-space development alongside engineers working across the hardware and software stack. Your contributions will help the wider software team use Graphcore hardware efficiently and support the systems our customers depend on. 

 Your tasks could include writing code, adding unit tests and manually testing your own and teammates’ changes. You’ll also help maintain continuous integration (CI) and fix issues, contributing to the work that keeps software development moving. 

 The team and culture 

 The Drivers and Utilities team sits within System Software, alongside Firmware and System QA. You’ll work with engineers who collaborate directly with Poplar SDK developers, silicon engineers and hardware engineers. 

 Technical design discussions, code reviews and Scrum sessions will help you understand how the team develops and coordinates its work. You can ask for help as you learn the codebase, discuss different approaches and use feedback to improve your changes. 

 Decisions are shaped by design discussions, code reviews and test results. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions, share ideas and flag problems early, with support from experienced engineers as you learn. 

 How you’ll learn and grow 

 Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build practical experience in low-level software development, testing and continuous integration through the work your tasks focus on. 

 Following changes from an initial idea through implementation and testing will help you understand what makes driver software reliable. You’ll learn how to check your work, investigate issues and contribute to a shared codebase, gaining a clearer view of a career close to the hardware. 

 Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated. 

 What we’re looking for 

 
 Currently studying for a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Maths, Machine Learning, Data Science or a related field 

 Low-level software experience, such as embedded code or device drivers, and introductory programming experience in C, C++ or Python. Personal or university projects count 

 Basic electronics knowledge, including the ability to read and understand schematics and datasheets 

 Awareness of continuous integration systems such as Jenkins, plus experience using Git to manage source code, raise and review pull requests, and merge branches 

 
 Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned. 

 Benefits 

 
 Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work 

 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship 

 Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista 

 Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform 

 
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. 

 We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you. 

 Sponsorship 

 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities. 

 Introduction to Graphcore 

 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. 

 An internship at Graphcore gives you the chance to explore where your interests and skills could take you. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. Together, you’ll share ideas and solve challenging problems, building experience and confidence to help you decide what comes next. 

 How to apply and what to expect 

 To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring. 

 Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.

 Start date: June 2027
 Applications deadline : Midnight, 29th November 2026 
 We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline. 

 The Internship Programme at Graphcore 

 Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence. 

 What you’ll be doing 

 Put your design skills to work making complex AI software easier for developers to understand and use. 

 As a UX Design Intern, you’ll create sketches, wireframes and interface designs for software that helps users understand, optimise and debug workloads running on Graphcore hardware. You’ll support usability research and help turn findings into insights that inform design decisions. 

 You’ll also create and refine components for Decagon, our design library, with guidance from the team. Your contributions will help make technical workflows more intuitive and give you a practical view of designing for a specialist audience. 

 Your team and support 

 The UX team works closely with engineers throughout software development. You’ll join sprint activities, design reviews and research, seeing how designers and engineers develop ideas together. 

 Your manager, Lucy, will work with you to build your skills, make time for learning and shape your career. Her favourite part of leadership is helping talented, driven people turn ideas into action, with the support and space to do their best work. You’ll also have a buddy to help you settle in, alongside a team of experienced designers keen to share what they know and help you develop. 

 Experienced designers and engineers will support you as you explore the UX lifecycle. You can ask for help as you develop your designs and use feedback to refine your work. 

 Decisions are shaped by research, feedback and open discussion. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions, speak up and try out ideas early, with support from experienced designers and engineers as you learn. 

 How you’ll learn and grow 

 Over the 12 weeks, you’ll explore how user-centred design principles apply to a technical product. Research and usability work will help you understand users’ needs, while sketches, wireframes and interface designs will give you ways to test and communicate your thinking. 

 Working on Decagon will help you understand how reusable components support consistent experiences. You’ll develop your judgement about what makes a design useful and gain a clearer sense of the UX work you’d like to pursue. 

 Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated. 

 What we're looking for 

 
 Currently studying towards a degree in UX, Interaction Design, Graphic Design, Computer Science or a related subject 

 Basic experience using design tools such as Figma or Adobe XD 

 A strong interest in UX/UI design and user-centred design principles, with a portfolio featuring coursework or personal projects, provided as a PDF or link 

 Clear communication, curiosity and willingness to learn from feedback 

 
 Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us about the problem you explored, the design choices you made and what you learned through your coursework or personal projects. 

 Exposure to technical products, user research or Agile working would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements. 

 Benefits 

 
 Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work 

 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship 

 Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista 

 Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform 

 
 We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. 

 We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you. 

 Sponsorship 

 Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities. . 

 Introduction to Graphcore 

 At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. 

 An internship at Graphcore gives you the chance to explore where your interests and skills could take you. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. Together, you’ll share ideas and solve challenging problems, building experience and confidence to help you decide what comes next. 

 How to apply and what to expect 

 To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring. 

 Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.
