ea3efd62aca6.description:
Career Area: 
Students and Graduates 
 Job Description: 
 Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc. 
 
 When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.
 
 12 Month Industrial Placement Scheme 
 Discipline: Design and Development Engineer
 Location: Peterlee, County Durham
 Salary: £26,000​, Share Scheme, Pension and 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays).
 
 At Caterpillar, you build what matters—whether it’s the career you want, crucial work skills, strong relationships, or new technologies. Our work is powered by our people.
 
 *Please note that in order to be eligible to complete a 12-Month Industrial Placement commencing July 2027, you must be in your penultimate year of study unless enrolled in an integrated master’s program. 
 
 Who is Caterpillar? 
 Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives. Operating from 50 countries around the globe and employing over 100,000 employees, the Caterpillar brand has developed into a symbol of strength, respect, and integrity. The organisation has a clear vision to be the global leader in providing customer value in the markets in which it operates. Our core values (Safety, Integrity, Excellence, Teamwork and Commitment) are key to our success.
 
 What do we do? 
 The Peterlee site is the only Caterpillar facility to design and manufacture Articulated Trucks, which are then exported globally. Our product design centre includes state of the art facilities with an immersive environment, machine proving ground, learning centre and complete factory which is the sole producer of Caterpillar Articulated Trucks.
 
 Diversity at Caterpillar 
 When we leverage our people's experiences, backgrounds, and cultures in an inclusive environment, we enable every individual to achieve their full potential, which drives business success. We are proud to be active partners with both the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) & Women's Engineering Society (WES). We also have numerous well supported employee resource groups. Caterpillar is an equal opportunity employer, and we welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds.
 
 What experiences can we offer you? 
 During your placement year you may be placed in one of the following engineering areas, working on live projects and continuous improvement activities:
 
 Machine Integration & Performance
 System Design & Integration
 Machine Testing and Development
 Product Support & Lifecycle
 Aftermarket, including Field Service & Maintenance
 Warranty
 
 Working with experienced team members you will receive all the coaching, guidance and support for your work and personal development. It is our intention that you will be given opportunities to develop your knowledge and experience within a real-world setting. Our aim is that these industrial placement opportunities provide the firm foundations necessary for a long and successful future career.
 
 The scheme will mentor you in the fundamental steps of deterministic design, the basics of machine performance, problem solving, development and validation, whilst learning the details of each subsystem.

 As an equal opportunity employer, we value diversity at Caterpillar, and we believe the more experience you can gain early in your career the further you can go.
 
 We operate a conditional offer process; our highest performing placement students are fast tracked to our graduate development scheme. This includes a financial incentive and the potential of a summer work placement. Offers will be made based on the condition that a graduate role is available at the time of your graduation and that you achieve a min of 2:2.
 
 Who are we looking for? 
 We are looking for engineers and scientists that will integrate Caterpillar Articulated Trucks with key technologies and data analytics. We are looking for people who can demonstrate technical knowledge and the practical application of engineering theory, along with sound decision making, professionalism, and an enthusiasm for engineering. You will also have strong planning and organising skills.
 
 Applicants will be on target to achieve a minimum of 2:2 honours degree level in the following disciplines: Agricultural, Electronics/Electrical, Computer Engineering, Mechanical and Mechatronics 
 
 Recruitment Process Guidelines: 
 We’re excited that you’re considering a career with Caterpillar. Below is an overview of our Early Careers recruitment process and what you can expect at each stage.
 
 Step 1 – Online Application: To apply, simply complete our online application form and upload your CV before the advertised closing date. Our team will review all submissions, and we’ll keep you updated and let you know as soon as possible if you’ve been selected to progress to the next stage.
 
 Step 2 – Online Assessments & Video Interview: If you are selected to move forward in the process, you’ll be invited to complete some online assessments, followed by a user-friendly video interview. Your responses will be reviewed by the hiring team, and successful candidates will then be invited to attend an in-person Assessment Centre, which we anticipate will take place on either Wednesday 9th December or Thursday 10th December at our Peterlee facility. If possible, we recommend keeping these dates available.
 
 To ensure you don’t miss any communications from us, please regularly check your text, email inbox (including your spam/junk folder) and your Workday account for updates.
 
 Step 3 – In Person Assessment Centre: Our Assessment Centre is designed to help you showcase your potential through a range of interactive activities focused on competencies such as teamwork, communication, problem-solving and decision-making.
 
 We aim to make the experience engaging, inclusive, and relaxed, giving you the best opportunity to demonstrate your strengths and learn more about Caterpillar.
 
 Step 4 – Offer: Following the Assessment Centre, the Caterpillar team will review all feedback to make hiring decisions. We aim to communicate outcomes and extend offers to successful candidates as quickly as possible.
 
 Placement students will begin their placement on 5th July 2027 .
 
 NOTE : Only one application is required, please do not apply for multiple roles. You may be given the opportunity of being considered for other roles/locations at a later stage.
 
 The panel cannot make assumptions when shortlisting therefore please demonstrate your qualifications and experience on your CV relevant to the criteria outlined. 
 
 Please note that this role requires a 5 day in the office model. 
 
 
This position requires working onsite five days a week. 
 
 
 
 
 Posting Dates: 
September 25, 2026 - October 25, 2026 
 
 Caterpillar is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants of any age are encouraged to apply 
 
 Not ready to apply? Join our Talent Community .

Job Description Summary 
In the 12-month Supply Chain Management Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience in covering all aspects of procurement, sourcing, logistics and supply chain management. 
 
 Job Description 
 About GE Aerospace 
 
 Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft . You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives . Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world! 
 
 Sourcing / Supply Chain 
 
 At GE Aerospace, our Sourcing and Supply Chain teams are a critical part of inventing the future of flight. Dedicated to finding the supplies and tools for our manufacturing and business processes. These teams work with a variety of supplier partners researching the best rates and negotiating contracts to support every step in our supply chain process. 
 
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 
 In this 12-month Supply Chain Management Placement , you'll gain hands-on experience in procurement, sourcing, logistics , supplier delivery, and supply chain management. 
 
 Your specific responsibilities will depend on your location and role. 
 
 You may work on supplier engagement, order management, tender reviews, cost reduction, inventory management, or logistics support. 
 
 You could collaborate on cross-functional process improvements, drive cost-out projects, and support initiatives like Product Cost and Defect PSR. Responsibilities could include data analysis, dashboard creation, problem-solving, and process optimization. You'll assist Operations Leaders with reporting, identify improvement opportunities, and ensure compliance with lean tools like Hoshin Kanri . 
 
 Role might involve project planning, lean manufacturing implementation, SQDC monitoring, and driving daily management activities to align with business strategy and achieve targets. 
 
 We have several types of roles in this area: 
 
 Lean/Process Improvement - Caledonian , Dowty & Wales 

 Materials and Planning - Caledonian & Cheltenham 

 Sourcing Projects - Cheltenham 

 Sourcing Fulfilment - Cheltenham 

 Business Operations (Supply Chain) - Cheltenham 

 Planning - Cheltenham 

 Supply Chain Management - Dowty 

 
 You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK.   
 
 This opportunity is offered in our Cardiff, Caledonian (Prestwick, Scotland) , Cheltenham, and Gloucester (Dowty , a GE Aerospace company) sites , during the process we will ask you to share your location and role preferences. 
 
 GE Aerospace Wales specialises in the maintenance, repair and overhaul of a range of commercial jet engines. The facility, based in Nantgarw, just north of Cardiff, occupies over 1.2 million square feet of workshop space and has two state-of-the-art aircraft engine test facilities, along with a significant repair capability – known as Component Repair Wales. 
 
 The site has the capability to provide maintenance, repair and overhaul services for a range of engine types – including the world’s most powerful commercial aircraft engine the GE90-115B and the world’s most popular commercial engine the CFM56 . 
 As one of the largest commercial aircraft engine maintenance facilities in the world, with annual sales of over $2bn, the business works with over 90 customers worldwide, including Emirates, TUI, Lufthansa, Delta, United, ANA and British Airways. 
 
 In 2017, the Wales site was selected as the Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility of choice for the GE9X; which will become the world’s largest and most fuel-efficient jet engine when it launches into service. The business will benefit from a £5m investment from the Welsh Government to support the total £20m investment put forward by the business, to equip and upskill the facility to be ready to maintain the GE9X fleet when it enters service on the new Boeing 777X aircraft. 
 
 The Wales team places a strong focus on providing career opportunities for talented individuals . Our apprenticeship, internship and work experience opportunities have been built to ensure the long-term success of our business by developing the next generation of technical, engineering and problem-solving talent. 
 
 GE Aerospace Caledonian is a purpose-built aircraft engine overhaul facility, adjacent to Glasgow Prestwick International Airport. The Caledonian site was officially opened in 1980 and has since grown into a centre of excellence for Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO) of CF6 & GEnx engine types. After each overhaul, the engines undergo intensive performance testing on site in our bespoke test cell, before returning to our global customer base ready for service. 
 
 Our vastly experienced and innovative workforce are passionate in the contribution towards the training of future engineers, leaders and surrounding talent in our organisation. At GE Caledonian, our Apprentices (Foundation, Modern & Graduate), XLP, OMLP and interns are key members of our team helping achieve the challenges of tomorrow. They continuously develop new skills to keep up with the pace of change in the Aviation Industry and become comfortable working in this ever-challenging environment which thrives on embracing change. 
 
 Our diverse team have a strong foothold in the local community, proactively seeking new volunteering opportunities to give back and deliver on our corporate responsibility. We have a dedicated affinity group on site who facilitate opportunities to the wider team, creating an inclusive culture we can all be proud of. 
 
 With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy.    
 
 Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge . Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come.    
 
 At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential.    
 
 Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight.   
 
 Dowty, a GE Aerospace company , is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for A wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft. 
 
 Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De-Haviland, Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J. 
 
 Operated by a highly skilled workforce, Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976; and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers. 
 
 This placement role is an intended pipeline to our Operations Management Leadership Progamme (OMLP) which is based across many of our UK sites. Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to secure a role prior to the end of their placement year. 
 
 Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above! 
 
 If you desire accelerated development to embrace opportunities in Operations, Supply Chain, Manufacturing and Quality, OMLP is for you. Find out more here https://invent.ge/omlp. 
 
 If you are passionate about Supply Chain Management, we would like to hear from you. 
 
 Qualifications / Requirements 
 
 Currently studying a Business/ Supply Chain Management/ Engineering/ Project Management/ Data Science / Computer Science / Digital Technology / Business Analytics / Materials Planning/ Operations Management Bachelor's or integrated Master's degree 

 Keen interest in Supply Chain Management 

 Good understanding of Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint 

 On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above 

 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement 

 
 Desired Characteristics  
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects  

 Organised & able to work towards deadlines  

 Inspired and curious to learn  

 Strong verbal and written communication skills  

 Able to take ownership for projects   

 Analytical and problem-solving skills   

 Proficient in Microsoft Office  

 Able to work as part of a team   

   
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact.  
 
 Total Reward  
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice , gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.    
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs.   
    
 Non-contributory Pension              

 Life Assurance   

 Group income protection                

 Private medical cover        

 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell   

 
 Recruitment Process   
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com . 
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31 st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.  
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too. 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS .    
 
 Right to Work

Job Description Summary 
In the 12-month Quality Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience in covering all aspects of quality from product & process design & definition, supplier quality, issue resolution and elimination through structured problem solving. 
 
 Job Description 
 About GE Aerospace 
 
 Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft . You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives . Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world! 
 
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 
 In the 12-month Quality Placement , you'll gain hands-on experience across various aspects of quality, including product and process design, issue resolution, and risk management. 
 
 Responsibilities will vary depending on the location and role, as each site has unique projects, production processes, and priorities . You could be involved in investigating quality issues, auditing products and suppliers, reviewing materials, analysing data or driving process improvements. 
 
 We have different types of roles in this area; here is a brief snapshot into each: 
 
 Supplier Quality (Chelte nham) - this role will identify improvement opportunities for the team, which will improve efficiency and productivity through already identified improvement projects and to help identify new opportunities for improvement. With support from the wider team, in this role you will have the opportunity to take on responsibility for the management of a small portfolio of suppliers from a supplier quality perspective to gain experience in supplier management in a business environment. 
 
 Product Quality Placement (Caledonian) - support the business in delivering defect-free aerospace engines to customers by participating in quality investigations, driving product safety risk reduction, and providing day-to-day quality support to operations. You help run proactive quality activities such as PFMEA, reduce quality escapes through improved defect detection and elimination, and contribute to the continuous improvement of the Quality Management System. You also work on improving quality communications and awareness across the facility, participate in staff and management quality forums, and perform trend analysis and action planning to address recurring issues and strengthen overall quality performance. 
 
 This opportunity is offered in our Caledonian (Prestwick, Scotland) and Cheltenham sites , during the process we will ask you to share your location and role preferences. 
 
 GE Aerospace Caledonian is a purpose-built aircraft engine overhaul facility, adjacent to Glasgow Prestwick International Airport. The Caledonian site was officially opened in 1980 and has since grown into a centre of excellence for Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO) of CF6 & GEnx engine types. After each overhaul, the engines undergo intensive performance testing on site in our bespoke test cell, before returning to our global customer base ready for service. 
 
 Our vastly experienced and innovative workforce are passionate in the contribution towards the training of future engineers, leaders and surrounding talent in our organisation. At GE Caledonian, our Apprentices (Foundation, Modern & Graduate), XLP, OMLP and interns are key members of our team helping achieve the challenges of tomorrow. They continuously develop new skills to keep up with the pace of change in the Aviation Industry and become comfortable working in this ever-challenging environment which thrives on embracing change. 
 
 Our diverse team have a strong foothold in the local community, proactively seeking new volunteering opportunities to give back and deliver on our corporate responsibility. We have a dedicated affinity group on site who facilitate opportunities to the wider team, creating an inclusive culture we can all be proud of. 
 
 With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy. 
 
 Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge . Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come. 
 
 At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential. 
 
 Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight. 
 
 If you are passionate about Quality (Products & Suppliers), continuous improvement and problem solving, we would like to hear from you. 
 
 This placement role is an intended pipeline to our Operations Management Leadership Programme (OMLP) which is based across many of our UK sites. Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to secure a role prior to the end of their placement year. 
 
 Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above! 
 
 If you desire accelerated development to embrace opportunities in Operations, Supply Chain, Manufacturing and Quality, OMLP is for you. Find out more here https://invent.ge/omlp. 
 
 Qualifications / Requirements 
 
 Currently studying a Business/ Data Analytics or Engineering/ Mechanical/ Aeromechanical degree or related Bachelor’s or integrated master’s degree 

 Keen interest in Quality/ Product Quality/ Supplier Quality 

 On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above 

 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement 

 
 Desired Characteristics 
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects  

 Organised & able to work towards deadlines  

 Inspired and curious to learn  

 Strong verbal and written communication skills  

 Able to take ownership for projects   

 Analytical and problem-solving skills   

 Proficient in Microsoft Office  

 Able to work as part of a team   

 
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact.  
 
 Total Reward  
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice , gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.    
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs.   
    
 Non-contributory Pension              

 Life Assurance   

 Group income protection                

 Private medical cover        

 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell   

 
 Recruitment Process   
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com . 
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31 st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. 
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too . 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS . 
    
 Right to Work   
 
 Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. 
 
 F urther, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website.

🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone. 

 We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

 After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us. 

 With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

 We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

 
 
 Software Engineering Internship (Summer 2027 ) 

 Closing Date: 1st of November 2026 

 📍London | 💰 £42,500 pro rata | Technology | L10 on the Engineering Framework 

 Engineering at Monzo 

 We have 500+ engineers across Monzo who design and build our in-house banking platform. We have big ambitions for the future, and technology plays a big role in creating a bank our customers want, so engineers at Monzo collaborate across disciplines to solve interesting challenges throughout the company.

 These range from the products our customers use everyday to underlying infrastructure, security, payments and finance, customer operations, financial crime, and data, to name just a few areas. As a bank, there is scope for impact across a huge number of opportunities.

 We contribute to open source software as much as possible. Our blog is a good place to learn even more about what we do.

 Engineering Interns 

 As a software engineer intern at Monzo, you’ll be matched with a team where you’ll spend the summer working on a real project for our customers. We’ll pair you with a mentor who will support you to design and ship a solution to solve a real problem.

 You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside engineers to learn more about software engineering and the types of challenges engineers at Monzo solve on a day-to-day basis.

 You’ll spend your internship:

 
 Writing, testing and shipping code that supports new features for our customers

 Reviewing code for your colleagues, to pick up any improvements and learn from your peers

 Working with product managers, designers and data analysts on your team

 Learning about new technologies, engineering practices and what a full-time software engineering role looks like

 Proactively seeking out feedback to improve and accelerate your learning

 
 What you’ll be using: 

 We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies:

 
 Go to write our application code (there’s an excellent interactive Go tutorial here )

 Cassandra for most persistent data storage

 Kafka for our asynchronous message queue

 Kubernetes and Docker to schedule and run our services 

 AWS for most of our production infrastructure and GCP for most of our data infrastructure

 React for our public web apps and internal tools

 Kotlin for our Android app

 Swift for our iOS app

 
 🤩 We’d love to hear from you if… 

 
 You are completing a degree in Computer Science or another technical field with exposure to programming and are graduating in 2028

 You enjoy learning about new technologies and have a passion for problem-solving

 You are available full-time for a minimum of 12 weeks between June and September 2027, we will have two June start dates to choose from

 You have the right to work in the UK without restrictions for the full 12-week internship and would not require visa sponsorship if offered a permanent position

 You can work from our London office on a hybrid basis to collaborate with your team and mentor, as well as attend intern events over the summer

 
 Please note you must hold the right to work in the UK through the full duration of this internship. 

 🙌What’s in it for you 

 💰£42,500 pro rata

 📍This role will be based in our London office on a hybrid basis (2 days per week in office)

 ⏰ We offer flexible full-time working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team 

 💻 Top-spec Macbook to use over the course of your time with us 

 🧠 Knowledge-sharing sessions with your squad and wider discipline 

 👯 Team and company wide socials / events 

 🍝 Lunch on Monzo twice a week from a range of street food vendors 

 🌈 The application journey has 3 key steps 

 Our application process involves three main stages:

 
 Submit your application with the short questions answered 

 If you’re successful, we’ll invite you to complete an exercise to demonstrate your programming and problem-solving skills

 If all goes well, you’ll have your final interviews with members of our engineering team via Google Meet

 
 The closing date for applications is 1st of November 2026, but we encourage you to apply as soon as possible as we will be extending offers on a rolling basis.

 We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. You can read them here. 

 Check out our blog to hear from our recent Interns.

 #EP-1
 
 Equal opportunities for everyone 

 Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog , 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report. 

 We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

 If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊

Career Area: 
Students and Graduates 
 Job Description: 
 Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc. 
 
 When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.
 
 12-Month Industrial Placement Scheme 
 Discipline: Manufacturing Engineering – Caterpillar Marine 
 Location: Wimborne, Dorset 
 Salary: £26 ,000 Share Scheme, Pension and 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays). 

 *Please note that to be eligible to complete a 12-Month Industrial Placement commencing July 2027, you must be in your penultimate year of study unless enrolled in an integrated master’s program. 
 
 
 What do we do? 
 Caterpillar Inc. is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines, and diesel-electric locomotives. Since 1925, we’ve been driving sustainable progress and helping customers build a better world through innovative products and services. Throughout the product life cycle, we offer services built on cutting-edge technology and decades of product expertise. These products and services, backed by our global dealer network, provide exceptional value to help our customers succeed.
 
 We have a clear vision to be the global leader in providing customer value in the markets in which we operate. Our core values (Safety, Integrity, Excellence, Teamwork and Commitment) are key to our success.
 
 Caterpillar, Wimborne 
 The facility boasts a wealth of hugely experienced designers, engineers and technicians used to providing solutions for commercial, professional and military customers in the marine product range. From design, testing and production, each engine is proven before leaving the premises to ensure the best performance for the end-user. The production products range up to 500 bhp for marine propulsion engines and 200 ekW for our gensets. In addition to the factory, the Wimborne location is home for roles across sales, marketing, product support and engineering for the entire range of Caterpillar marine products.
 
 Diversity at Caterpillar 
 When we leverage our people's experiences, backgrounds, and cultures in an inclusive environment, we enable every individual to achieve their full potential, which drives business success. We are proud to be active partners with both the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) & Women's Engineering Society (WES). We also have numerous well supported employee resource groups. Caterpillar is an equal opportunity employer, and we welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds.
 
 What experiences can we offer you? 
 As an equal opportunity employer, we value diversity at Caterpillar and believe the more experience you can gain early in your career the further you can go. That’s why during our yearlong scheme we place an emphasis on multiple diverse projects. You will have the opportunity to work and collaborate with people in Caterpillar facilities worldwide and we are looking for you to bring fresh, innovative ideas to solve complex technical problems. You will be a fully involved team member with responsibility and accountability for key business deliverables. That said, you will be given all the support you require to be successful.
 
 Our placement roles have the additional benefit of a workplace mentor; this could be your manager or a technical expert who will support you throughout your time at Caterpillar and help you gain the professional development and skills you need to be set up for success! Our placement students can expect to return to university with further developed technical skills and experience of how University learning is applied to the workplace.
 
 We also operate a conditional offer process; our highest performing placement students are fast tracked to our graduate development scheme. This includes a financial incentive and the potential of a summer work placement. Offers are based on the condition that a graduate role is available at the time of your graduation and that you achieve a minimum grade of a 2:1 Degree.
 
 The role 
 With the business growing we are looking for a manufacturing engineering placement student at Caterpillar Marine, located in Wimborne, Dorset within the Caterpillar Oil, Gas & Marine Division (COGMD). The Manufacturing Engineering team supports the production of marine engine & genset products ranging from 10kW to over 750kW. This role will focus on ensuring efficient, on-time production of a wide range of marine power products.
 
 Manufacturing Engineering placements offer real life production support experience in a customer-focused environment.
 
 Job duties and responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: 
 Supporting the production of marine engines, generators and associated equipment. 
 Participating in projects for new product introduction (NPI). 
 Resolving production related problems. 
 Component & sub-assembly production routings. 
 Learning and applying the Caterpillar Production System (CPS). 
 Liaison with shop floor operators and designers on the assembly / manufacture of product. 
 Conduct all work in accordance with company policies and procedures. 
 
 Who are we looking for? 
 We’re looking for people who can show us a highly collaborative working style, and who thrive in a team of committed professionals. At the same time, we need people who are self-motivated and can drive change through persuasion and influence. Communication and presentational skills are essential.
 
 As the type of roles within our business are becoming more diverse, we are looking for people who are open minded, excellent problem solvers and who have an ability to learn quickly. You will be motivated, diligent, and will embrace change. In return for your dedication and hard work, you will be provided with excellent career opportunities and strong support for your personal and career development to pursue a career within Caterpillar.
 
 Applicants will be on target to achieve a minimum of 2:1 honours degree level in a relevant discipline:
 · Production Engineering
 · Manufacturing Engineering
 · Mechanical Engineering
 · Automotive Engineering
 · Aerospace Engineering
 
 
 Recruitment Process Guide 
 We're excited that you're considering a career with Caterpillar. Below is an overview of our Early Careers recruitment process and what you can expect at each stage.
 
 Step 1: Online Application 
 To apply, simply complete our online application form and upload your CV before the advertised closing date.
 Our team will review all submissions & we'll keep you updated and let you know as soon as possible if you've been selected to progress to the next stage.
 
 Step 2: Online Assessments & Video Interview 
 If you’re selected to move forward in the process, you'll be invited to complete some online assessments, followed by a user-friendly video interview. Your responses will be reviewed by the hiring team, and successful candidates will then be invited to attend an in-person Assessment Centre/Interview, which we anticipate will take place on Wednesday 9th December 2026 at our Wimborne facility . If possible, we recommend keeping this date available.
 
 To ensure you don't miss any communications from us, please regularly check your text, email inbox (including your spam/junk folder), and your Workday account for updates.
 
 Step 3: In Person Assessment Centre 
 Our Assessment Centre is designed to help you showcase your potential through a range of interactive activities focused on competencies such as teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making.
 We aim to make the experience engaging, inclusive, and relaxed, giving you the best opportunity to demonstrate your strengths and learn more about Caterpillar.
 
 Step 4: Offer 
 Following the Assessment Centre, the Caterpillar team will review all feedback and make hiring decisions. We aim to communicate outcomes and extend offers to successful candidates as quickly as possible.
 
 Placement students will begin their placement on 5th July 2027.
 
 We look forward to receiving your application and wish you the very best throughout the recruitment process. Come join us!
 
 How do I apply? 
 Go to catukgraduates.com for more information. 
 
 NOTES: 
 · The panel cannot make assumptions when shortlisting therefore please demonstrate your qualifications and experience on your CV relevant to the criteria outlined.
 · Pending the number of applications, the criteria for the position may be enhanced to facilitate shortlisting. This may also include an adjustment to the application deadline date.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Posting Dates: 
September 25, 2026 - October 25, 2026 
 
 Caterpillar is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants of any age are encouraged to apply 
 
 Not ready to apply? Join our Talent Community .

 At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything.  Johnson & Johnson is currently recruiting Placement Students for our Integrated Data Analytics and Reporting (IDAR) function. We are recruiting for the following department: Clinical and Statistical Programming (C&SP). The position is for university students who will be looking to complete a 12 month industry placement.
 We are seeking highly motivated candidates to join our pharmaceutical research department. The successful candidate can gain invaluable hands-on experience in analysis helping advance our medicines in development at Johnson & Johnson.
 We are seeking an innovative Clinical & Statistical Programming Placement Student to join our team, offering hands-on experience in analysis tools for data integration, automation, and clinical insights. Collaborate with experts to support projects that enhance operational efficiency and meet business needs. As a C&SP Placement student, you can leverage AI-based programming to design and develop statistical solutions for clinical research analysis and reporting, or create AI-driven technology tools to support C&SP.
 
 How you can make a difference: Make an impact by applying your understanding of data structures and AI programming (SAS, R, and Python) techniques to analyze trial data and craft innovative solutions tailored to business needs.
 
 Upon successful completion of your training your main responsibilities may include (but not be limited to): 
 Work with Clinical & Statistical Programming counterparts applying analyses in an array of disease areas. 
 Conduct research to identify innovative solutions that can be applied to our business processes. 
 Collaborate with team members to design and develop solutions using SAS, R, Python, RPA, Power Automate and other tools. 
 Create and maintain documentation for solutions. 
 Stay up to date with emerging technologies and trends. 
 
 
 Qualifications: 
 · Ability to effectively apply knowledge and skills in a complex environment.
 · Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
 · Good written and verbal communication skills.
 · Good problem solving and decision making. 
 · Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 · Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
 Familiarity with programming languages such as SAS, R, Python, and others. Exposure to Data Bricks, LSAF, SAS Enterprise, and other Data Science platforms is a plus. 
 Education Requirements:

Job Description Summary 
In the 12- month Programme Management Placement, the successful candidate will join our Customer Programmes team which supports civil and military customers of our propeller systems for airborne and amphibious applications. 
 
 Job Description 
 About GE Aerospace 
 
 Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft . You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives . Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world! 
 
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 
 In the 12-month Programme Man a gement Placement offers diverse roles within the function, with responsibilities tailored to the specific needs of different teams. While all roles focus on program management, customer support, and operational efficiency, tasks will vary based on team priorities and projects. 
 
 Responsibilities may include: 
 
 Coordinating customer requests such as RFQs and purchase orders, ensuring deadlines are met through collaboration with supply chain and engineering teams, preparing customer order books, facilitating client calls, and ensuring high satisfaction and timely delivery. 

 Support Program Management Reviews (PMRs) by managing calendars, preparing agendas, and tracking actions. 

 Leading process improvement projects to enhance operational efficiency, implementing Lean principles, and analysing operational data to create performance metrics that drive team focus on strategic priorities. 

 Cross-functional collaboration is a key aspect of the role, working closely with Operations, Sourcing, Engineering, and Quality teams to meet customer and business objectives . Some teams may focus on facilities and maintenance, including asset reviews, day-to-day operations, contractor control, and long-term projects to support stakeholders. 

 
 We have opportunities within: 
 
 Field Services (Dowty) - managing internal metrics, financials, materials, pricing models, and logistics , with broad exposure to satellite sites and international field locations. The role involves tracking KPIs (such as turnaround times, schedule adherence, utilisation, and cost performance), maintaining dashboards and reports, and supporting root cause analysis of performance issues. You will assist with financial tracking (revenue, costs, margins), support pricing model updates, help manage materials data, and contribute to cost analysis for continuous improvement. On the operational side, you will coordinate logistics information, support planning for field activities, and maintain documentation so stakeholders stay informed. The role requires close collaboration with Programmes, Finance, Operations, and Logistics, including supporting cross-functional reviews and small improvement projects in reporting, data quality, and process flow. The placement offers end-to-end exposure to field service operations, practical experience in metrics, financial and logistics coordination, and development of professional communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills. 

 
 Facilitates & Maintenance Projects (Caledonian) - learning maintenance management and continuous improvement in a business operations environment, covering preventive and reactive maintenance, preventive maintenance planning, compliance, sustainability projects, and environmental monitoring and gap analysis. Monitoring performance metrics, identifying improvement opportunities and developing project management skills through small- to medium-scale projects. The role requires adapting to different people and environments daily, understanding departmental challenges to set maintenance priorities, communicating with various stakeholders and responding to critical needs, and learning from experienced staff to improve existing processes and work-scopes. Also working with suppliers and contractors during preventive maintenance to ensure high safety standards, gain exposure to shift supervision and maintenance management, and collaborate with internal and external resources on sustainment and environmental improvement projects. 

 
 Military Platforms (Cheltenham) - broad range of program management, customer support, order management, and cross-functional business improvement activities within a military-focused organisation. The role is designed to give the intern practical experience in managing internal special projects, supporting customer engagement, and becoming familiar with program management practices, procedures, internal systems, and standard work. The placement will work closely with stakeholders, customers, and colleagues across multiple functions, while contributing to business-focused projects, driving actions to closure, presenting findings and recommendations, and developing communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills. 

 
 BizJet Portfolio (Cheltenham) - you will gain exposure to the complete program and product lifecycle, from new product introduction through to repair and overhaul services. The programs team you will join is a dynamic and growing portfolio, offering a strong opportunity to contribute to day ‑ to ‑ day program activities and develop core program management skills. Key activities include reviewing customer purchase orders and supporting the Program Team in managing the product orderbook, ensuring alignment between customer portals and internal order management systems. You will support sales and operational review meetings through orderbook management and engagement with key stakeholders involved in demand changes. You will help with obsolescence management by developing regular reviews with key functions, monitoring stock run ‑ out dates, and improving communication with other programs where obsolescence risk is shared. You will act as a “voice of the customer ”, supporting communication between internal teams and the customer, engaging with customers to help secure invoice payment in support of cash targets, and helping to organise and support program review meetings with customers. 

 
 OE Value Stream Programs (Dowty) - focuses on planning, coordinating, and delivering manufactured spare parts to ensure reliable aftermarket support. The role owns the integrated production and delivery plan for defined part families, aligning production and materials with customer demand and business priorities, and applying a structured operating model to meet Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost objectives . Working cross ‑ functionally with materials planning, manufacturing, quality, sourcing, logistics , and customer ‑ facing teams, the role manages production schedules, monitors performance, addresses risks and issues, and keeps customers informed through clear, proactive communication on delivery status, changes, and recovery plans. It combines operational planning, data ‑ driven performance management, and customer relationship management to improve delivery reliability and overall supply chain effectiveness. 

 
 Programme Management Office (Cheltenham) - supporting the successful delivery of complex projects from early bid and concept stages through to closure. The PMO Project Controller is responsible for managing budgets and schedules using standardised tools, maintaining integrated project plans, and providing analysis to identify and mitigate cost and schedule risks. The role serves as a key point of contact for project management tools and practices, coaching project and technical leaders and performing earned value analysis to support informed decision-making. It also supports structured change and risk management processes, including preparing change documentation, participating in risk and opportunity reviews, and ensuring decisions are clearly recorded. In addition, the PMO Project Controller contributes to accurate project forecasting and helps coordinate resource plans across multiple teams to ensure projects are appropriately staffed and controlled. 

 
 Programme Management (Cheltenham) - This role offers a strong development opportunity in program management best practices by applying daily management and lean principles across all workstreams of one of our programmes. The individual will be responsible for maintaining robust document control across NPI, production execution and aftermarket, coordinating actions with the integrated program team (IPT) following tollgate reviews and key meetings, and ensuring all program risks and opportunities are captured and managed in the digital thread tool. The role also includes monitoring and reporting touch labour and material performance against targets, identifying opportunities to eliminate non ‑ value ‑ added work using lean principles and project management principles. Through these activities, the individual will gain hands-on experience in quality assurance, QMS, risk management, and end-to-end program execution. 

 
 You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK. 
 
 This opportunity is offered in our Caledonian (Prestwick, Scotland), Cheltenham, and Gloucester (Dowty, a GE Aerospace company) sites , during the process we will ask you to share your location preferences. 
 
 GE Aerospace Caledonian is a purpose-built aircraft engine overhaul facility, adjacent to Glasgow Prestwick International Airport. The Caledonian site was officially opened in 1980 and has since grown into a centre of excellence for Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO) of CF6 & GEnx engine types. After each overhaul, the engines undergo intensive performance testing on site in our bespoke test cell, before returning to our global customer base ready for service. 
 
 Our vastly experienced and innovative workforce are passionate in the contribution towards the training of future engineers, leaders and surrounding talent in our organisation. At GE Caledonian, our Apprentices (Foundation, Modern & Graduate), XLP, OMLP and interns are key members of our team helping achieve the challenges of tomorrow. They continuously develop new skills to keep up with the pace of change in the Aviation Industry and become comfortable working in this ever-challenging environment which thrives on embracing change. 
 
 Our diverse team have a strong foothold in the local community, proactively seeking new volunteering opportunities to give back and deliver on our corporate responsibility. We have a dedicated affinity group on site who facilitate opportunities to the wider team, creating an inclusive culture we can all be proud of. 
 
 With over 1,700 employees, GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy.   
 
 Our heritage dates back to 1940 yet our technology is cutting-edge . Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of state-of-the-art aircraft power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical aircraft systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come. 
 
 At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships, mentoring and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential. 
 
 Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight.   
 
 Dowty, a GE Aerospace company , is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for A wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft. 
 
 Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De-Haviland, Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J. 
 
 Operated by a highly skilled workforce, Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976; and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers. 
 
 If you are passionate about Programme Management, we would like to hear from you. 
 
 Qualifications/Requirements 
 
 Currently studying a Business Administration/ Project Management/ Finance/ Data/ Engineering or Program Management related Bachelor’s or integrated Master’s degree 

 On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above 

 To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement 

 
 Desired Characteristics 
 
 Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects 

 Organised & able to work towards deadlines 

 Inspired and curious to learn 

 Strong verbal and written communication skills 

 Able to take ownership for projects 

 Analytical and problem-solving skills 

 Proficient in Microsoft Office 

 Able to work as part of a team 

   
 A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact. 
 
 Total Reward  
 
 At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible. 
 
 As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs. 
   
 Non-contributory Pension 

 Life Assurance 

 Group income protection 

 Private medical cover 

 Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell 

 
 Recruitment Process 
 
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process. 
 
 If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com . 
 
 Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31 st O ctober but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. 
 
 Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too. 
 
 Security Clearance 
 
 Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS . 
 
 Right to Work   
 
 Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. 
 
 Further, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website. 
 
 Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward. 
 
 
 Additional Information 
 Relocation Assistance Provided: No

NXP Semiconductors, Automotive Processors, Solutions & Applications, Glasgow, UK, (3 month Summer Internship) 
 
 The mission:
 The car is becoming a computer on wheels, and AI is moving from the cloud to the edge; right onto silicon. Our S32N automotive MPUs pack proprietary AI IP blocks that let carmakers run machine learning where it matters: in the vehicle, in real-time, safely.
 
 We're looking for an AI-native intern — someone who reaches for an LLM, a notebook, or a model as second nature — to spend time with our Glasgow team working on real edge-AI problems with real automotive silicon.
 
 What you'll actually do:
 Get hands-on with our S32N MPUs — helping prepare, optimise and deploy ML models onto real hardware.

 Prototype AI use-cases and help turn them into demos.

 Write clean, modern code and use AI coding assistants and automation as everyday tools.

 Learn alongside a global network of experienced engineers who'll help you grow fast.

 
 What we're looking for:
 A 3rd or 4th year student working towards a degree in Computer Science, Electronics, AI/ML, Software or a related field.

 Familiarity with AI/ML basics and Python — and genuine curiosity about LLMs and modern AI workflows.

 Some software fundamentals (any C/C++ a bonus) and comfort with version control (git).

 A builder's mindset: you like learning by doing and aren't afraid of a problem without a textbook answer.

 Clear communication and enthusiasm to jump in.

 
 Why it's worth it:
 You'll get real experience at the ground floor of edge AI in automotive — real silicon, real problems, and a team that'll back you to experiment, learn, and bring us fresh thinking we don't yet have.

fa558417fc8d.description:
Cambridge, UK | Full-time | Fixed-term, 10–12 weeks | Hybrid

 Salary: £30,000–£35,000 per annum, depending on experience, paid pro rata for the internship duration.

 About us 

 Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion. 

 Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.  

 About the role 

 Our full-time summer internships give current students in technical fields the opportunity to apply their skills and expertise in an industrial setting. 

 You will join us at our head office in Cambridge, UK, for 10 to 12 weeks, working alongside talented software and hardware engineers, mathematicians, quantum information theorists and physicists who are experts in their fields. 

 You will have a dedicated supervisor and work on a project designed to make the best use of your existing skills while developing your knowledge of quantum computing and quantum error correction. We will support you in producing a meaningful piece of work that you can be proud of by the end of your internship. 

 Previous interns have committed code to industry-standard open-source compilers, co-authored research papers and led the design of new software tools. 

 What you will do 

 
 
 Design, develop and test software that contributes to Riverlane’s quantum error correction technology.



 
 
 Work closely with colleagues across software engineering, research and other technical disciplines 

 
 
 Explore ideas, evaluate different approaches and contribute to technical problem-solving 

 Communicate your work clearly through discussions, presentations and written reports 

 Develop your understanding of quantum computers, quantum error correction and their potential applications 

 
 What we need 

 
 
 You must be a current student at the time of application, studying towards a Bachelor’s degree (second year or later), Master’s degree or PhD.



 
 You must be studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Electronic Engineering or another related technical subject.



 
 Experience using at least one general-purpose programming language, demonstrated through coursework, personal projects or research.



 
 An understanding of core programming concepts, including data structures and algorithms.



 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.



 
 Clear written and verbal communication skills.



 
 The ability to take initiative and work effectively as part of a team.



 
 An interest in applying your software skills to quantum computing; prior quantum computing knowledge or experience is not required.



 
 Availability to work full-time for 10–12 weeks.



 
 Even better if… 

 
 
 You have experience with C++ or Python, the main languages you will use during the internship.



 
 You have experience writing tests, debugging code or using version control tools such as Git.



 
 You have developed software as part of a collaborative project.



 
 Important notes 

 
 
 You must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the internship. If you hold a UK student visa, please check that its conditions allow you to undertake this full-time internship.



 
 
 PhD students may need to temporarily step away from their PhD to complete the internship. This may affect their right-to-work status, and applicants should check their individual circumstances 

 
 
 You must be available to work full-time for 10 to 12 weeks during the summer vacation period 

 
 
 You will be required to sign an agreement assigning ownership of any intellectual property produced during your internship to Riverlane 

 Internships are based at our head office in Cambridge, UK 

 
 How to apply 

 Please upload a CV and covering letter through our careers page. Your CV should include the grades you have received so far in your degree(s). Your covering letter should explain why you are applying for the software engineering internship and what skills and experience you would bring.

 Deadline 

 Please submit your application by Friday 6 November 2026 . Interviews will be held in Cambridge, or virtually if required.

 What can you expect from us 

 Alongside a competitive salary, we offer private medical insurance, a health cash plan and life assurance, as well many other benefits. 

 You can also expect a diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 25 different nationalities. 

 If you have any queries, please contact jobs@riverlane. com . Please do not send your applications to this email address, all applications should be submitted via our careers page. 

 Everyone is welcome at Riverlane. We are an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from eligible and suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender reassignment, religion or belief, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, or pregnancy and maternity/paternity. 

 Women and other underrepresented groups may be less likely to apply for a role unless they meet all or nearly all of the requirements. If this applies to you, we still encourage you to apply - you may be a great fit, even if you don’t meet every single qualification. We’d love to hear from you. 

 If you need any adjustments made to the application or selection process so you can do your best, please let us know. We will be happy to help. 

 GDPR notice: Riverlane collects and processes personal data in accordance with applicable data protection laws. If you are a European Job Applicant see the privacy notice for further details.
